## 0. What v1 is — DECLARED versus BUILT

> **Read this before you read anything else in `model/`.** Since 7 Aug 2026 the
> scope of v1 is a **decision**, not an aspiration, and roughly a third of the
> model is deliberately inert. A stranger who does not know this will read a
> declared-and-unbuilt type as a commitment.

**The ruling, and it is the whole mechanism:**

- **`drop_for_v1`** means the type **stays declared in `model/`**, carries a dated
  note, and gets **NO table, NO endpoint, NO code**. It is **not deleted**.
- **`delete`** means removed from the tree. In the entire v1 pass there is
  **exactly one** — `ROLE_KEYS` and the `RoleKey` type, 7 Aug 2026.

**How to tell, in one line, without reading a diff.** Every dropped declaration
carries this comment immediately above it:

```
/** @dropped-for-v1 7 Aug 2026 — <one line of why>. Declared, not built. */
```

The note **on the declaration** is the authority, because it travels with the code
and cannot go stale separately from it. Two whole modules — `presentation.ts` and
`deployment.ts` — additionally carry a ⚠️ banner at the top of the file saying the
whole module is dropped, why that is safe, and what would trigger restoration.

**Counts, each with the command that reproduces it** (re-run by hand 8 Aug 2026,
evening — ⚠️ **and this is the Markdown TABLE form, which
`tools/check-doc-counts.mjs` cannot see at all**, because the number sits in a
different cell from the noun. **Nothing but a person checks the three numbers
below.** The first of them was stale by two when this was re-run):

| | | Command |
|---|---:|---|
| `@dropped-for-v1` occurrences in `model/` | **230** | `grep -rho '@dropped-for-v1' model/*.ts \| wc -l` |
| …of those, sitting directly on a top-level `export` | **198** | `awk '/@dropped-for-v1/{f=1;next} f&&/^export /{c++;f=0;next} f&&NF{f=0} END{print c}' model/*.ts` |
| total `export` declarations in `model/` | **795** | `grep -h '^export ' model/*.ts \| wc -l` |

> ⚠️ **10 Aug 2026 — THE EXPORT NUMBER ABOVE IS KNOWN STALE AND IS BEING LEFT
> ALONE DELIBERATELY. Do not "fix" it in this commit.** Run the command: at
> `HEAD` the tree derives a larger figure than the 795 stated, and in the
> *working* tree it is larger again — 834 — because a concurrent session has
> `model/observability.ts` modified and uncommitted along with a **fourth**
> OpenAPI file, `docs/contracts/data-plane-local.openapi.yaml`, that is not yet
> tracked. `node tools/check-doc-counts.mjs` therefore reports export,
> contract-operation and contract-path lines across the record as stale, **and
> it is right**; every one of them is stale against a tree nobody has committed.
> **The sweep belongs to whoever lands that fourth contract file**, in the same
> commit, because a number written now against the working tree would be wrong
> the moment it is committed against `HEAD`. This is §5.11 **inverted** — a count
> broken by a checker that was correct, rather than a checker fooled by a count.

The **32** remaining notes (230 less 198) are **field-level and union-member-level** drops (a field
on a live interface, a member of a live union), plus a handful of prose mentions
inside doc comments that reference the marker rather than being one — for example
`governance.ts` records that `SubjectLocation.trace` **survives** the trim and is
deliberately *not* annotated. **The split above is approximate by construction;
the per-module reasoning is `docs/v1-scope-ledger.md`.**

Whole modules dropped: **`presentation.ts`** (52 notes — dashboards and the
builder) and **`deployment.ts`** (13 — the fleet, under G36, which slips BYOA to
v1+1). Heaviest partial drops: `learning.ts` 33, `billing.ts` 32, `domain.ts` 30
(**29 until G102's `palette` landed on 8 Aug** — `grep -c '@dropped-for-v1'
model/domain.ts`),
`evaluation.ts` 21.

**Why nothing was deleted, in one sentence:** `model/identity.ts` names 17 dropped
types across 60 sites, so under a deletion reading the totality proofs stop
compiling — and two of the three invariants a survival pass marked BROKEN come
back as merely **UNENFORCED** instead, which is a much cheaper state to be in.

⚠️ **Two things a dropped note does NOT mean.** It does not mean the type is
wrong, and it does not mean nothing depends on it. `docs/v1-scope-ledger.md` §6
lists the invariants that are now declared-and-unexercised rather than enforced —
invariant 9 (nothing in v1 can roll back a fleet at all) chief among them.

⚠️ **Nothing checks a drop note.** No tool in this repository can tell whether a
`@dropped-for-v1` note is on the right declaration or whether its stated reason is
true. `tools/planner/extract.mjs` is blind to it — a comment above a declaration
changes no edge. The only verification of the trim's *content* is a human reading
the ledger against the model.

**Full reasoning, module by module, with the restorations argued:**
`docs/v1-scope-ledger.md` — itself a **dated snapshot, banner-marked unmaintained**
under G32.

### 🟢 9 October 2026 — V-3 DEPLOYED: THE `controlapp` SECRET NOW NAMES `reconcile_control_app`, AFTER ONE DEPLOY FROM A STALE CHECKOUT WAS CORRECTED

**This entry covers #609 and #610 and the hand deploy that followed. A record
slice wrote it on 9 Oct 2026 (G4476).** The code argument is G4471's and is not
repeated. Written against `origin/main` @ `d3bf9820`:

```bash
git log --first-parent --oneline d626275e..d3bf9820 | grep 'Merge pull request'   # #610 d3bf9820 · #609 1f003038
git show bf2e13d4:infra/lib/data-stack.ts | grep -c "'ControlReader'"             # 2 — the reader secret still declared before #606
git show d3bf9820:infra/lib/data-stack.ts | grep -c "'ControlReader'"             # 0
grep -n "ROTATION_ROLE_NAME\|const CONTROL_APP_ROLE" infra/lib/data-stack.ts      # one spelling, 'reconcile_control_app'
```

**Reported by the orchestrator, measured on staging 9 Oct 2026, and NOT
re-measured by this slice** (no AWS call was made here):

- **Both pipeline runs Succeeded** — for #609 and for #610.
- **The stuck `AWSPENDING` version `8a160693…` on
  `reconcile-staging-controlapp` was removed first.** Only the label was
  removed; the rotation was NOT cancelled.
- 🛑 **INCIDENT — THE FIRST `cdk deploy reconcile-data-staging --exclusively`
  RAN FROM A LOCAL `main` THAT HAD NOT BEEN PULLED (G4478).** It sat at
  `bf2e13d4`, before #606. That deploy RE-CREATED the control-reader secret
  (`ControlPlaneControlReader`), its resource policy, its rotation Lambda, role,
  log group and schedule — and did NOT carry #610. The reader role is `NOLOGIN`
  and revoked by control migration `0052`, so the recreated secret
  authenticated nothing, and no alarm fired. About 15 minutes later `Data` was
  redeployed from `d3bf9820`; `DescribeSecret` on the reader secret answers
  `ResourceNotFound` again.
- **The corrected deploy:** the `reconcile-staging-controlapp-rotation`
  function's `ROTATION_ROLE_NAME` is `reconcile_control_app`, and so is the
  secret's username. **CloudFormation DID generate a new password** — new
  `AWSCURRENT` `643a191b…`, old `944eca5b…` now `AWSPREVIOUS` — as G4471 warned.
- **Then pipeline execution `59b9cabc…` Succeeded**, and its Migrate stage set
  the role's password from the new secret.
- ⚠️ **The pipeline did NOT restart the control plane, because the image tag
  had not changed (G4479).** A new control-plane deployment was forced at
  13:37 +08. It logged *"listening … as reconcile_control_app"*, and the next
  tenant-name pull through the control plane wrote 2 of 2 with no auth error.
- **`probe-staging` passed 8 of 8.** The only alarm in `ALARM` is the
  demo-intake DLQ, since 4 Oct (V-1, unchanged).
- ⚠️ **The rotation itself was NOT exercised (G4480).** It refuses while its
  holders run, by design (G3923). The first real test is the scheduled run on

#### What actually got built

`contract/`, `control-plane/`, `data-plane/`, `dev/` and `http/` — Fastify with
**the four OpenAPI tiers as the router and the validator** (G191), **two
processes and two databases in `compose.yaml`** so invariant 3 is held by
topology rather than by discipline (G193), and a **local-only signed test token**
behind one flag with no permissive default (G192). `model/` is now **on the
served path**, `getRun` is mounted, and a request body is validated **from the

(capability), `checkLocalHealth` (dataPlaneLocal), `listEntitledPacks`

#### The owner's four decisions of 16 August, taken after all of the above

**These change what the next session does and one of them settles a question this
entry would otherwise have left open.**

**Ⓐ G200's MECHANICAL CLAUSE GOVERNS, so PR #259 STANDS.** The operative test is
**"mounts a new HTTP operation"**, not the headline *"no further operation is
served"*. **Serving more through an operation that is already ungated is
permitted until the authorisation pass lands.** ⚠️ **G200's row already carries
this and it is easy to miss under everything else in the cell** — *"The freeze is
on MOUNTING, not on declaring … A PR that registers a handler is [in conflict]"*
— **but #259's own title reads *"and every one of them UNGATED"*, and the two
readings genuinely differ.** **#259 is not to be recorded as an open question and
not to be reverted.** The next agent will meet the same ambiguity; the answer is
this paragraph.

**Ⓑ THE NEXT AGENT IS AUTONOMOUS ON UNBLOCKED WORK ONLY.** It works issues that
need no ruling, red-teams and merges PRs, and **stops at anything gated on a
decision.** That is the standing mandate.

**Ⓒ THE CI TOKEN MINTER GETS BUILT NEXT SESSION** — see *what to do next*, item 1.

**Ⓓ FOR THE PENDING RULINGS: THE NEXT AGENT PROPOSES A DEFAULT FOR EACH AND
PROCEEDS UNLESS THE OWNER VETOES.** 🛑 **THIS IS NOT RECORDED AS A CLEAN WIN AND
THE RISK IS STATED FIRST, BECAUSE THIS ENTRY IS THE EVIDENCE AGAINST IT.** The
record's own position is that architectural decisions are the owner's, and
**this session produced three cases where the orchestrating agent's read was
wrong and only a question caught it** — ① the foundation tier, ② the green check
without a database, ③ the inflated counts. **Under propose-and-veto each of those
three would have LANDED rather than been caught.** So the terms that make a veto
cheap are part of the ruling, not a gloss on it:

- **Every proposed default is minted as a G row that NAMES ITS REJECTED
  ALTERNATIVE, states what it costs, and is written to be reversible.** A default
  with no rejected alternative on the row is not a default; it is a decision
  taken quietly, and G60 is what that costs — *recorded as applied, with the
  thing it authorised still impossible*, for eight days.
- 🛑 **ANYTHING TOUCHING AN INVARIANT, A CAPABILITY, A PLANE BOUNDARY OR A
  CREDENTIAL IS NOT A CANDIDATE FOR A PROPOSED DEFAULT. It goes to the owner
  regardless.** That excludes the authorisation pass's capability choices, S-2's
  RLS key, anything reaching `secret` or `statutory`, and anything that would put
  a foundation service on a network.
- **A default that has been live for a week without a veto is still a default.**
  Say so on the row, or the veto window becomes a silence that reads as assent.

### The three things to do next, in this order

1. **BUILD THE CI TOKEN MINTER.** Owner decision Ⓒ, taken 16 Aug 2026: **an
   instance profile plus a GitHub App private key in SSM Parameter Store, and a
   runner loop that mints its own registration token before each `config.sh`.**
   🛑 **The cost was accepted explicitly and is recorded rather than glossed: a
   GitHub credential lives in AWS.** It is an **App key scoped to this repository
   and rotatable — NOT a PAT**, which is the whole of why it is acceptable. ⚠️
   **The two current mitigations are stopgaps and must not be mistaken for the
   fix**: four runners per launch buys **four jobs**, and SSM being online makes a
   token refresh a one-command push rather than a new instance. **Neither removes
   the one-hour cliff; they only make hitting it cheaper.** Note that this key
   lands on the same host where pull-request code executes under `instanceRole`,
   so **it belongs in SSM read at boot, never in an environment variable and
   never on disk in the workspace.**

### 🟢 12 August, LATER THE SAME DAY — THE GATE TOOK THE FIFTH CHECKER, THE DROP DETECTOR WAS FOUND LYING, AND G185 SPLITS THE DATABASE BY REGION

🛑 **STILL NOT ON `main`.** Everything below is on `docs/c4-model-and-plane-rulings`
and, at the time of writing, **uncommitted in the working tree**. `main` is still
`50991c12`.

**Four green/red design passes were run over the C4 record and adjudicated.** Two
constructive (container/plane topology; persistence and schema) and two adversarial
(attack the two-instance premise; attack the C4 record and its generator). The
owner's opening premise — *two database instances, one per plane* — **was refused on
the plane axis and granted on the region axis**; that ruling is **G185** in §3, and
it amends decision F rather than replacing it. Read the row before touching `db/`.

**Three defects were found and TWO ARE FIXED.**

1. 🛑 **The drop detector marked SEVEN LIVE EXPORTS as `@dropped-for-v1`, and the
   page drew them in red.** `isDropped()` matched the tag **anywhere** in any
   leading comment, so a declaration was marked dropped **because its neighbour's
   drop was narrated in prose above it**. The exports:
   `SubjectLocation`, `POLICY_KINDS`, `LivePolicyKind`, `NormalisationReader`,
   `mayPromoteLearning`, `TelemetryPlane`, `AUTOMATED_ROLLBACK_EXISTS`. The best of
   them is `SubjectLocation`, **whose own comment says it is NOT annotated — and the
   page marked it dropped for saying so.** §5.1, keyed on the landmark instead of the
   property, inside the tool built to depict the tree. **Fixed:** the tag must open a
   line, and only the declaration's own (last) comment range is read. **Dropped count
   203 → 196.** Derive the separation:
   `grep -h '@dropped-for-v1' model/*.ts | grep -cE '^[ \t]*(\/\*\*?)?[ \t]*\*?[ \t]*@dropped-for-v1\b'`
   → 223 annotations against 235 occurrences, the 12 remaining all prose.
2. 🛑 **`tools/planner/extract-c4-data.mjs` CONTAINED A RAW NUL BYTE AND WAS
   THEREFORE INVISIBLE TO `grep`.** One literal NUL, used as a dedupe-key separator
   at what is now `:240`. `file` reported *binary data*; every `grep` over the
   extractor returned **silence rather than an error**. In a record whose whole
   verification culture is *derive it, run the grep*, the C4 extractor was the one
   file a grep could not see into, and it failed quietly. **Fixed** by writing the
   escape `\u0000` — same string, same generated bytes, and the file is text again.
   ⚠️ **Nothing in `npm run check` detects this class**; it was found only because a
   grep that should have matched returned nothing.
3. 🟢 **THE EXPORT COUNTS NOW AGREE AT 849, AND THE FIX WAS NOT THE OBVIOUS ONE.**
   They read **849 / 198** against **826 / 196** — two mechanical derivations of one
   noun, 23 apart, both green in the same gate. The 23-export gap was exactly the
   `export type { … }` **re-export statements**, which the AST walker had no branch
   for — so `extract-c4-data.mjs`'s claim to emit *"every top-level export"* was
   **false by 88 names**, across **23 re-export statements**. ⚠️ **This line briefly
   read *87*: one adversarial pass counted 87 and a second counted 88, and the 87 was
   taken on trust and written in before being derived. It is 88 — the miscount came
   from a regex that missed one multi-line statement. Two agents disagreeing is not a
   count; the loop below is.**
   🛑 **AND ADDING THE 88 NAMES TO THE TOTAL WAS THE WRONG FIX — IT OVERSHOT TO 913.**
   That is the same defect wearing the opposite sign, and it is worth stating because
   it is the trap anyone repeating this work will fall into: **849 and 913 are two
   different nouns.** `grep -c '^export '` counts export **statements**, and one
   re-export statement is one line however many names it carries; the page's Level 4
   lists **names**. The extractor now publishes **both** — `totals.exports` **849**,
   matching the governed derivation exactly, and `totals.exportedNames` **913** — and
   Level 4 gained the 88 names it had been silently omitting. ⚠️ **A first attempt
   derived the statement count from the set of distinct source modules and read
   839, because two statements may re-export from the same module. Count the
   statement where you parse it.** ⚠️ **The DROPPED figures still differ — 196 from
   the extractor against 198 from `check-doc-counts.mjs` — and that gap is NOT
   closed.** It is a semantic difference, not an arithmetic one: the awk derivation
   resets on the second line of a multi-line JSDoc, and the AST reads the
   declaration's own comment range. **Two remain unaccounted for; do not write either
   number into prose as though it were settled.** Derive the export figures:
   `node -e "const fs=require('fs');let s=0,n=0;for(const f of fs.readdirSync('model').filter(x=>x.endsWith('.ts'))){const L=fs.readFileSync('model/'+f,'utf8').split('\n');for(let i=0;i<L.length;i++){const r=L[i].slice(7).trim();if(!L[i].startsWith('export ')||!(r.startsWith('type {')||r.startsWith('{')))continue;s++;let b=L[i],j=i;while(!b.includes('}')&&j<L.length-1)b+='\n'+L[++j];n+=b.slice(b.indexOf('{')+1,b.indexOf('}')).split(',').map(x=>x.trim()).filter(Boolean).length}}console.log(s,n)"`
   Worse: `tools/check-doc-counts.mjs` scans `*.md` only, so

#### 🛑 THE PLAN WAS WRONG FOUR TIMES AND EACH IMPLEMENTATION CAUGHT IT

Recorded as a **pattern**, not as four incidents, because the next plan will be
written by somebody who trusts plans. `docs/build/wave-two-plan.md` is a careful
document and it was wrong in four independent ways:

1. **C18's spec duplicated five arms into a second union** — §5.3, two vocabularies
   for one concept, in a plan written to close an integrity gap. Refused by the
   implementation, which uses **one** wrapping arm carrying a `PopulationDefect`.
2. 🛑 **C13's spec required two properties that CANNOT BOTH HOLD.** §7.4 demanded
   that a rate above the ceiling REFUSES *and* that a wholly-refused side returns
   `ok: true` carrying `population_wholly_refused`. A wholly-refused side is
   **10000 basis points**, which exceeds every legal ceiling because the upper
   bound is exclusive — so the refusal always fires first, the post-condition is
   **UNREACHABLE and its fixtures impossible to write**. The repair: the rate arm
   requires at least one ADMITTED row (`model/reconciliation.ts:3766`).
3. **O-15's mutation (c) turns nothing red** — the two things it contrasts agree
   today, because `presentedRows` derives one header-grain row from a zero-line
   document. The test says so rather than claiming coverage it does not have.
4. **Two file-count estimates were wrong, and both commit splits failed the same
   way.** C18's ③a/③b and C13's split did not hold, because **a required input
   field re-breaks the same files in every half.**

> ⚠️ **A mutation that cannot fail is not a test, and this wave says so out loud
> four separate times.** Where a planned mutation turned nothing red, the finding
> was written into the test file rather than smoothed over. That is the habit
> §5.6 exists to enforce.

#### 🛑 TWO PROOF MECHANISMS WERE FOUND WEAKER THAN WHAT THEY PROVED — the week's most important finding, and it is about neither control

- **`AssertNoTextDeep` banned the TYPE `string` and admitted TEN string-bearing
  escapes** — `ReadonlySet<string>`, `ReadonlyMap<number, string>`,
  `{ describe(): string }`, `() => string`, `Uint8Array`, `ArrayBuffer`, `Date`,
  bare `object`, a constructor-signature type, and **a class whose only field is
  private**. 🛑 **And its container coverage was LUCK.** `Set`, `Map`, `Promise`,
  `WeakMap`, `Error` and `RegExp` were caught **only via
  `[Symbol.toStringTag]: string`** — an incidental member the readonly twins do
  not have. **Nobody chose that boundary, and a boundary nobody chose is not a
  control.** Inverted under G146 (`model/reconciliation.ts:326`).
- **O-15's own reachability assertion was VACUOUS on first draft.** Written
  `T extends true ? true : never`, it **COMPILES when it resolves to `never`** —
  §5.6 arriving inside the mechanism written to prove §5.2 is closed. Rewritten
  as `Assert<T extends true>` and verified RED both ways (`TS2344`) before being
  trusted green — `tests/model/reconciliation-empty-population.test.ts:353`
  and `:357`.

**Both were inside mechanisms written to prove something else was closed.** The
generalisation, and it is the sentence to carry out of this week: **a proof
mechanism is not exempt from the defect classes in §5, and it is the one artefact
nobody thinks to attack.** Neither was caught by review. Both were caught by
deriving the escape list again rather than trusting the one already written down.

#### 🛑 AND ONE CONTROL CANNOT BE WITNESSED BY ANY TEST — this repository cannot see the class at all

O-15's mutation (b) is the §5.2 defect ported faithfully: move the escape from
the binding (`model/reconciliation.ts:1268`) to a run-level parameter, across all
six construction sites. **It turns ZERO tests red. 880 of 880 still pass.**

The control's whole value is **REACHABILITY** — who can reach the off-switch, and
at what cost — and **reachability is structural**. No runtime fixture can witness
it, because both spellings compute the same answer for every input. Only a
compile-time assertion can hold it, which is why O-15 ships two.

> 🛑 **A repository that proves its controls with fixtures alone cannot see this
> class at all.** §5.2 catalogues *a caller-supplied parameter that switches a
> check off*; the whole of `tests/` would stay green through the introduction of
> one. **Where a control's value is that a parameter does NOT exist, the guard is
> a type, and a green suite is not evidence.** ⚠️ And note the ordering trap the
> C16 split found at the same site: a `@ts-expect-error` must sit on the
> **offending field**, not above the `export const` — an excess-property error is
> reported at the property, so a directive on the declaration is unused
> (`TS2578`) while the real error still fires and **the test passes while
> asserting nothing.**

#### ⚠️ A COPY OF THE RUN-STATUS ENUM CAN NEVER BE PINNED, AND O-16 WILL WALK INTO IT

#### ⚠️ THE RECORD'S OWN APPLIED-COUNT COMMAND IS NOW UNSOUND — §5.11, in the derivation rather than the number

The command this record and `CLAUDE.md` both ship —
`grep -E '^\| G[0-9]+ \|' docs/HANDOFF.md | grep -c '✅'` — counts a ✅ **anywhere
in the row**, including the consequence cell. On 11 Aug `a0d18522` put four ✅
verification marks inside **G145's** consequence cell while its status stayed
`not applied`, so **the naive command now over-reports by exactly one.** Derive
the status cell instead:

```bash
grep -cE '^\| G[0-9]+ \|' docs/HANDOFF.md                                 # 183 rows
grep -E  '^\| G[0-9]+ \|' docs/HANDOFF.md | grep -c '✅'                  # 38 — OVER-COUNTS, see above
grep -E  '^\| G[0-9]+ \|' docs/HANDOFF.md | sed -E 's/\\\|/~/g' \
  | sed -E 's/.*\|([^|]*)\|[[:space:]]*$/\1/' | grep -c '✅'              # 37 applied
```

⚠️ **The `sed -E 's/\\\|/~/g'` step is load-bearing and is not tidiness.** Several
status cells quote a union containing an escaped pipe — `'queued' \| 'running'` —
and without that substitution the second `sed` splits inside the cell and the
count comes out **33**, wrong in the other direction. **A derivation command is
as capable of being subtly wrong as the number it replaces**, which is G109's own
argument arriving in a shell pipeline.

**Applied moved 36 → 37 in this pass** — one row, **G172**, and the evidence is in
its own consequence cell. ⚠️ **`CLAUDE.md` still carries the naive command and is
not this file's to fix.**

### How to typecheck the model

There is no local `tsc` in this repository — **again**. There was one only while
the deleted application's `node_modules` happened to be installed, and the 6 Aug
cut removed `package.json` along with the rest of the root build config, so
nothing here will ever install one. The working method:

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/tscheck
npm --prefix /tmp/tscheck install typescript@5.9 --no-save
cp /Users/jrkphani/Projects/Reconcile/model/*.ts \
   /Users/jrkphani/Projects/Reconcile/model/tsconfig.json /tmp/tscheck/
```

Then, **as its own command** — not chained onto anything:

```bash
/tmp/tscheck/node_modules/.bin/tsc -p /tmp/tscheck/tsconfig.json; echo "EXIT: $?"
```

**The copy step is optional.** Verified 6 Aug 2026: the throwaway compiler runs
against the repository's own config in place, which removes a whole class of
error — a stale copy in `/tmp` typechecking clean while the real file does not.
Also as its own command:

```bash
/tmp/tscheck/node_modules/.bin/tsc -p /Users/jrkphani/Projects/Reconcile/model/tsconfig.json --noEmit; echo "EXIT: $?"
```

Returns `EXIT: 0`. `model/tsconfig.json` has `"include": ["*.ts"]`, so it picks
up all 18 modules relative to itself, wherever the compiler binary lives (*"sixteen"*
until 10 Aug 2026).

> **`cd` inside a compound Bash command silently swallows this.** A
> `mkdir … && cd … && tsc …` chain does not run the compiler in this harness, and
> it does not tell you it did not. It returns an exit status that looks like
> success. Run the compiler on its own line, with absolute paths, and read the
> `EXIT:` line. Verified clean at `6711cf2f`: exit 0 under `strict`,
> `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `erasableSyntaxOnly`,
> `verbatimModuleSyntax`, `noUnusedLocals` and `noUnusedParameters`
> (`model/tsconfig.json`) — stricter than the application's own settings.

consequence is what the next person actually needs.

trunk cut and the v2 screen pack — twenty-two decisions, **almost none applied**.

Replaced by `REQUIRES_ENUMERATION` (`model/governance.ts:354`), which is **stronger** — a delivery grant may name tenant data only with a non-empty instance list, and the list may now name a document, an exception **or a run**. | A | **Admission gated by role plus classification** | `minimumRoleToAdmit` default `operator`; an agent ceiling by data class; a second person above a class. `mayAdmit()` decides | `model/policy.ts:449` · `docs/domain-model.md` §14.3 |
| A | **An admitting agent carries no tools** | The agent that admits is never the agent that acts, so injected text cannot induce its own admission | `docs/prompt-injection-posture.md` §4 |
| A | **Trifecta rule validated at pack signing** | No untrusted→outbound path without a human step, and the human step must declare `correspondence` in `requiredEvidence` — kind alone made the control satisfiable with a rubber stamp. A rule that only fires in production is a rule that ships broken | `model/domain.ts:657` |
| A | **Three new foundation services** | F12 Sanitisation (out-of-process, no credentials, no egress), F13 Tool Broker, F14 Authoring Validator. F13 exists because a component must not enforce its own limits — tool scope was being enforced inside Mastra | `docs/prompt-injection-posture.md` §5.4 |
| A | **Injection corpus is not a `SeededExample`** | A probe asserts an *absence*. No partial credit, `waivable: false` in every environment, and a live failure returns `compliance_violation` — deliberately bypassing the scorer-level rollback rule, because a safety regression is not quality drift | `model/evaluation.ts:417,457` |
| A | **Acquisition fidelity is modelled** | `expectedFidelity` vs `actualFidelity`, four tiers. The *gap* is the signal: invoices structured last quarter and scanned this one are a supplier problem, not a model-tuning one | `model/domain.ts:876` |
| A | **Autonomy is recommended from measured dials, never applied** | Reversibility declared; blast radius and frequency observed; verifiability inferred from reversal rate, evidence rate and median decision time — where a *fast* decision is a warning, not a reassurance. `recommendAutonomyCeiling()` narrows on thin evidence and widens only on thick | `model/policy.ts:514,625` |
| A | **Risk appetite belongs to the tenant** | An FDE may propose the initial setting; only a tenant role may own it thereafter. `AutonomyDecision.decidedBy` is a tenant user | `docs/domain-model.md` §14.7 |
| A | **Not every reversal indicts the autonomy** | `reversalIndictsAutonomy()` is a function, not a comment, because a call site that quietly counts *all* reversals drives autonomy to `none` across the fleet while producing a chart that looks like evidence | `model/domain.ts:1668` |
| A | **A third environment posture: `evaluation`** | Behaves as production for every invariant, and adds a recorded processing agreement (null blocks non-synthetic ingest), an agreed purge date, and no entitlement lease. Conversion to production is deliberate and never automatic. The synthetic-only sandbox rule is untouched | `docs/data-governance.md` §2.1 |
| A | **`TenantContact` names a duty, not a person** | People leave, and a named individual who has left makes escalation fail silently at three in the morning. Reach only — authorisation stays with `Membership`, because only support-grant approval is an authenticated act | `model/domain.ts:472` · `docs/domain-model.md` §14.10 |
| A | **Stakeholders, capabilities and scope replace the `RoleKey` enum** | Four layers, each a closed set defined by the one above. A pack or tenant composes roles and **neither can invent a capability** — which is what stops role authoring becoming a second, unreviewable authorisation system beside the policy engine | `model/access.ts` · `docs/domain-model.md` §15 |
| A | **A role carrying zero capabilities is legitimate** | The `sponsor` class. A CFO who owns the close and never opens an exception needs to be kept in the loop, not granted access — so a sponsor role resolves to a notification binding | `docs/domain-model.md` §15.1 |
| A | **Scope is five fixed dimensions, conjoined** — ⚠️ **six since E** | `domains` · `definitionIds` · **`solutionIds`** · `costCentres` · `legalEntities` · `valueCeiling`. Not arbitrary key/value, because that is a second policy engine with its own evaluation order and its own ways of being wrong. The sixth is what `definitionIds` was already doing one level down, by hand (`model/access.ts:553`). ⚠️ **Two of the six bind on nothing** — `Exception` carries no cost centre and no legal entity, so that narrowing typechecks and does nothing (§11.10) | `model/access.ts:528` · `docs/domain-model.md` §15.4, §16 |
| A | **Deny is not representable** — ⚠️ **superseded by D, read §8.6 before quoting this** | True of the *capability read path* and false of the system: twelve negative predicates exist across four layers, three of them explicit deny lists including `neverExport`, commented *"whatever the role"*. The replacement claim is narrower and checkable: **every prohibition is either a narrowing or the removal of an authority** | `docs/access-and-agency.md` §2, §8.6 |
| A | **Agents hold no roles** | `AGENTS_HOLD_ROLES = false` (`model/access.ts:1930` — the `:556` cited here previously no longer resolves). The argument is lifetime: a role is standing and per-principal; a step's `toolScope` is per-step, per-run and signed inside a pack the injection validator gated. A role-holding agent is never probed, because the validator tests procedures, not principals | `docs/access-and-agency.md` §3 |
| A | **Six things called hierarchy collapse to two mechanisms** | Cost-centre and legal-entity trees are one `ScopeHierarchy` over an existing dimension; approval chains are an ordered ladder, not a tree; reporting lines are **deleted** rather than relocated | `docs/access-and-agency.md` §1 |
| A | **Narrowing is automatic; widening is an act** | The rule the codebase already had twice (`recommendAutonomyCeiling`, `purgeVerdict`). Hierarchy produces three more instances and all three fail identically without it — someone gains authority as a side effect of an administrative act nobody reviewed as a grant | `docs/access-and-agency.md` §1 |
| A | **Role inheritance, a durable agent registry, a general delegation graph, deny rules, DAGs and an account-level access role are all refused** | Each with a stated reason. Do not reintroduce one without reading the table | `docs/access-and-agency.md` §4 |

### Pass D — 5 Aug, afternoon: the organisation axis, federation, the stress test

Nineteen decisions across three sections. Full reasoning in
`docs/access-and-agency.md`; the consequences that change other people's work:

| | Decision | Consequence | Recorded |
|---|---|---|---|
| D | **A third access axis: `OrgClass`** — platform · partner · customer | Not a field on `Role`. A property of an *evaluation*, derived from (principal, tenant) at session establishment. The old `RoleKey` enum was doing **three** jobs, not two — `partner_admin` was an organisation baked into a role name, which is why the two partner-clamp functions could not be migrated | §8, `docs/access-matrix.html` |
| D | **Stakeholder classes renamed** | `author · administrator · user · sponsor · assurance`. Three renames have framework backing (NIST, ITIL, IIA/Basel/COBIT); `operator` was rejected outright — zero presence in any framework and it means a controller in Kubernetes. **Open and recorded, not resolved:** ITIL nests `sponsor` inside service-consumer alongside `user`, so those two are peers in a set where the reference standard says one contains the other | §8.1 |
| D | **Customers author values, never expressions** | The permission document is a **serialised projection** — generated, signed, versioned; TypeScript stays the source of truth; **no parser admits a hand-written document as an authority**. Customer configuration is a form over a closed schema. This is what collapses the missing administration tier from ~120 CRUD operations to ~16 | §8.2 |
| D | **Federation: customers and partners bring their own IdP** | `IdentityProvider` (a *kind*) becomes `IdentityConnection` (an *instance*, with an `owner`), and org derives from `connection.owner`. `User.isStaff` is deleted — it is derived. Verified: there is **no SAML, OIDC, SSO, federation or SCIM anywhere in the repo**, which is a procurement blocker before it is a model gap | §9 |
| D | **Support access is pre-authorised at contract time** | A standing customer authorisation names purpose, resource classes, max hours and who may invoke; each incident draws against it. Reuses `EntitlementLease`'s shape and its honest limit — withdrawal stops future draws, not live ones. `MAX_GRANT_HOURS` becomes negotiated per customer, and must start being *read* | §8.5, §10.2 |
| D | **Notifications are first-class reads** — with one carve-out | A content-bearing digest is masked, scoped, classified per channel, audited and residency-checked. **Operational notices to a `TenantContact` are service communication, not reads** — without that carve-out, `customerNotifiedAt` is never set and every support grant fails forever | §8.4, §10.1 |
| D | **Two new resource classes** — ⚠️ **thirteen in total since E** | `authority` (autonomy, roles, user admin) reachable only where the contract pre-authorises it; `statutory` in neither permitted list. Closes the verified hole where a 90-day delivery grant that provably cannot read tenant data could rewrite the rules deciding who reaches tenant data | §8.7, §11.2 |
| D | **Three deny lists invert** | `neverExport → exportable`, `neverAutonomousIn → autonomousIn`, `blockInOutput → permitInOutput`. The polarity is the prize: `neverExport: []` is permissive, `exportable: []` is restrictive. The same fix `AssignmentScope` already received and the policy config never did | §8.6 |
| D | **Consent requires the delta, not the whole role** | `canGrant` asks the right question for a grant and the wrong one for a consent — it deadlocked the only person who could accept a widening upgrade. The delta check is also what closes the **proxy escalation**: widen a colleague's role, consent to it, and nobody who holds the capability ever agreed | §10.4 |
| D | **Roles do not revert with a pack** | Behaviour reverts on an automated safety rollback; authority stays at `min(v_n, v_n+1)`. Without this a failed injection probe widens live authority at 04:00 with no human in the path — *narrowing is automatic, widening is an act*, inverted by the safety machinery | §10.5 |
| D | **A policy's author is provenance, not a live authority** | Organisations outlive employees. **Only safe because** acceptance mints a policy owned by a *tenant* user — which makes the propose-and-approve path load-bearing rather than optional | §10.3 |

**Three items moved from *recorded* to *blocking* — a decision now rests on each:**

- **`AutonomyProposal` and the propose-approve path.** §10.3 is only safe if an
  FDE is never a policy author. `recommendAutonomyCeiling()` structurally cannot
  recommend at onboarding, because `sampleSize` is zero.
- **`mintedRoleIds` on `InstalledPack`.** §10.5 is not expressible without it —
  an install cannot currently record what a pack minted, so a rollback could not
  un-mint it.
- **A closed list of service-notice kinds.** §10.1 is a hole rather than a
  carve-out until it exists.

**Two additions that land in closed sets, so they are cheapest now:** capability
**31** for digests (§10.6, deliberately *not* `view_dashboard`, which sits inside
a partner mask), and the **`configure_identity`** resource class (§9.4a, split
out of `authority` so a regulated customer can withhold one and still have SSO).

**Decided against the recorded advice, and the argument is preserved:** a
break-glass path for `place_legal_hold` (§10.7), scoped to preservation only.

### Pass E — 5 Aug, evening: the resource axis, the spine, agents and dashboards

Full reasoning in `docs/access-and-agency.md` §11 and `docs/domain-model.md` §16.
Two new modules — `model/agents.ts` and `model/presentation.ts` — take the count
to **thirteen**.

| | Decision | Consequence | Recorded |
|---|---|---|---|
| E | **A fourth access axis: resource class** | The axis existed for **one org class out of three** — a staff grant had a resource term; a customer role and a partner assignment had none. So a delivery grant saying *"no tenant data"* and a role saying *"manage_roles"* had **no vocabulary in common**, and nothing could tell that the second sat outside the first. `CAPABILITY_RESOURCE_CLASS` is the join, `Record<Capability, …>` and zero logic — an unclassified capability is a compile error | `model/access.ts:517` · §11.1 |
| E | **Thirteen resource classes, each carrying a rule true of it and false of its neighbour** | `tenant_data · configuration · authority · statutory · identity · endpoint · secret · substrate · commercial · catalogue · schedule · metering · telemetry`. Resemblance was rejected as a test because the drift it permits is unfalsifiable | `model/governance.ts:141` · §11.2 |
| E | **`sample_data` is removed** | It was `tenant_data` under a selector. `REQUIRES_ENUMERATION` replaces it and the safety property **strengthens**: delivery cannot reach tenant data *it has not been handed instance by instance*. Reverses a pass-A decision | `model/governance.ts:354` · §11.3 |
| E | **Four capabilities added — 31 to 34** | `view_summary`, `configure_identity`, `bind_secret`, `enable_endpoint_writeback`; `configure_connection` becomes `configure_endpoint`. **33 closes a live hole:** `configure_connection → configuration`, and delivery reaches `configuration`, so a 90-day delivery grant could bind the customer's ERP credentials | `model/access.ts:251` · §11.2 |
| E | **`configure_telemetry` moves to `authority`** | `TelemetryPolicy.maxDataClassInSpanAttributes` is a classification ceiling; set to `sensitive_personal` alongside `includeExplanations: true`, the one class delivery may read becomes a full exfiltration path. Delivery reaches `telemetry` by design and must not set what lands there | `model/access.ts:472` · §11.2 |
| E | **One `Endpoint` registry, direction as a flag** | Replaces four unrelated lists — the same verification rule was enforced twice and not at all twice, and Slack/Teams installs were modelled nowhere. Not two classes: *a mailbox you send to and a mailbox you poll are the same mailbox*. What differs is the gate — inbound is a trust boundary, outbound a disclosure surface | `model/domain.ts:519` · §11.4 |
| E | **The authorisation spine** | `authorize()` mints an `AuthorizationGrant`; `redeemAuthorization()` re-derives on presentation. `authorizationId` now joins `AuditEvent`, `DataAccessEvent` and `UsageRecord` — three streams that previously **could not be joined at all**, with the middle one not stored. **A reference, not a bearer token:** possession is not authority, and a fired employee's in-flight acts stop on the next call rather than at the next expiry | `model/access.ts:1461,1555` · §11.6 |
| E | **`AuditEvent` and `DataAccessEvent` are hash-chained and anchored** | Metering was sequenced, chained and signed because a customer-owned plane could under-report; the record of **who touched a data subject's data** had none of it, in the same database under the same root. `ChainAnchor` ships the head hash only — a scalar carrying no tenant data, so invariant 3 holds. ⚠️ **THAT LAST CLAUSE BECAME CONDITIONAL ON 10 Aug 2026 AND THE DECISION THIS ROW RECORDS IS OTHERWISE UNAFFECTED.** G145 adds a **partition** field to `ChainAnchor`, and whether the anchor still carries no tenant data **is a property of the axis, which nobody has named** — a fixed small bucket keeps the claim, an axis derived from actor or subject breaks invariant 3 on its face. **So invariant 3 on the anchor is not "preserved" and not "broken"; it is UNDECIDABLE until the axis is named**, which is condition (a) of G145's amendment. 🟢 **THE AXIS WAS NAMED ON 11 Aug 2026 AND THE SENTENCE ABOVE IS LEFT STANDING AS THE HISTORY IT IS.** The owner ruled a **fixed bucket count, `0..N-1`** — the one candidate `docs/build/chain-partition-verification.md` §2.4 scores ✅ on invariant 3 — so the undecidable reading is **closed in the favourable direction**: on that axis the anchor still carries no tenant data. ⚠️ **But it is closed as a DECISION, not at the tree** — no `partition` field and no axis exist in `model/` (`grep -rn 'partition' model/*.ts` → 13 hits, all unrelated), and **N now rides on the anchor too**, so read the amended G145 row in §3 before restating this clause | `model/governance.ts:1110,1138` · §11.7 — ⚠️ **these citations read `:906,934` until 10 Aug 2026 and BOTH STILL RESOLVED**, to a `customerApprovedAt` field and to a line inside a different function's docblock. `RecordChain` and `ChainAnchor` moved and the citations followed nothing; `tools/check-citations.mjs` cannot catch this class because the citation *resolves*. Reproduce: `grep -n 'export interface RecordChain\|export interface ChainAnchor' model/governance.ts` |
| E | **`Solution` — the tenant-side operating assembly** | `SolutionPack` (catalogue) → `InstalledPack` (minting record) → `Solution` (what runs). Everything an operator calls *"the AP reconciliation"* had no object, so there was nothing to disable, hand to a partner, scope to, or roll back | `model/domain.ts:1860` · §11.8 |
| E | **A solution is a scope, never a grant** | `SOLUTION_IS_GRANTABLE = false`. **The assembly contains a secret** — it reaches an `Endpoint`, which carries a `credentialRef`, and `secret` is in neither permitted list and is non-delegable. ⚠️ **That last clause went FALSE on 8 Aug 2026 — G75 put `secret` in `PERMITTED_RESOURCES.delivery` and removed it from `NON_DELEGABLE_RESOURCES`. The decision this row records is UNAFFECTED**: `SOLUTION_IS_GRANTABLE = false` because granting a container atomically confers everything inside it in one act, and that argument never depended on `secret` being unreachable — it depended on the grant being *atomic and unreviewed*. The premise moved; the conclusion stands. Granting the container atomically would confer in one act something no grant may confer at any price. `AssignmentScope` gains a sixth dimension instead, which intersects and can only take authority away | `model/access.ts:1971` · §11.8 |
| E | **Agents compose from model, tools, harness and evals** | All four closed. Tools become a closed vocabulary with `TOOL_EFFECT` total over it — no `http_request`, no generic escape hatch, and no tool that resolves a credential. `PlatformAgentEvalFloor` is a floor **the pack cannot see**, because `SolutionPack.gateIds` let a pack name its own examiner. Provenance resolves the contradiction between `prompt-injection-posture.md` §5.4 and `tenancy-topology.md` §4: editing a pack agent's harness converts it to tenant-authored | `model/agents.ts` · §11 |
| E | **A dashboard is a composition; the canvas is `configuration` and each binding is a `tenant_data` read under the *viewer's* scope** | `view_dashboard` and `view_summary` gated a noun that did not exist. **Opening the canvas does not confer the contents** — two users with different scopes see different numbers. Refuses the category default (Tableau embedded credentials, Power BI fixed identity, Looker PDT owner), where a saved view is a standing scope-bypass wearing a chart | `model/presentation.ts:975,1094` |

(`model/domain.ts:2451`), the fold into one `decide()` (`model/access.ts:985`),
and `CAPABILITY_RESOURCE_CLASS` (`model/access.ts:517`) — items 1, 1c and 1d of

Contrast `UsageAttestation`, which has both a submission path and a `/usage/attestations/chain-head` resume endpoint (`docs/contracts/control-plane.openapi.yaml:381`). **(c) is owed work with a named blocker; (a) and (b) are decisions rather than code, and their window is this one.**<br><br>⚠️ **THE COST SENTENCE IN THIS ROW IS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE RATHER THAN DELETED, BECAUSE IT IS THE SENTENCE A READER WOULD HAVE TRUSTED.** It reads *"verification must walk every partition, so 'a missing row' becomes a per-partition claim rather than a whole-stream one."* **A missing ROW does become a per-partition claim, and that half is benign** — it is the same claim over a narrower domain, with identical detection, identical proof and identical cost. **A missing PARTITION becomes an UNCLAIMABLE one, and that is not a weaker version of the old claim — it is a NEW HOLE where there was none.** Unpartitioned, gap detection is **INTRINSIC**: delete rows 500–510 and rows 499 and 511 survive **in the same chain** and bracket the hole, needing no anchor and no second party — and the set of chains is closed **IN THE TYPE**. Drop a whole partition and nothing brackets anything: no surviving `previousHash` points into the hole, no sequence skips a number, every surviving chain verifies perfectly, and **nothing enumerates the partitions**. `RecordChain`'s own sentence is the one to hold it against — *"absence of a row is invisible without it"* (`model/governance.ts:1112`) — because partitioning re-creates invisible absence one level up. **In the dispute this decides, *"no such record exists"* and *"the partition holding it was dropped"* produce BYTE-IDENTICAL evidence:** unpartitioned a customer who re-canonicalises under RFC 8785 and walks 1..head against the anchored head can state *"the stream is complete"*; partitioned as ruled, the strongest sentence available is *"every stream I was shown is complete"* — **and in a dispute about a removed record the holder chooses what is shown.** 🟢 **Struck with it: *"verification must walk every partition"* IS NOT A COST AT ALL.** N chains totalling L rows cost L−N hash comparisons against one chain's L−1, and N independent chains verify **in parallel** where one is strictly serial. The real cost was never walking the partitions — it is **knowing which ones to walk**. ⚠️ **The same wrong sentence is carried by `docs/build/stateless-adjudication.md:780` and its draft row `:1219`, and by `docs/build/stateless-application.md:1475` (*"a slightly weaker claim"*) — RECORDED HERE, NOT EDITED**, because those are committed design records and not this file's to rewrite.<br><br>🟢 **WHAT SURVIVES THE AMENDMENT — said plainly, because an amendment that lists only damage misleads.** Edit detection; rewrite detection via the anchor; **the unrecordable-act claim**, which rests on the chain at `model/access.ts:1450`; **`ChainAnchor.id` itself**; and **G20's canonicalisation, untouched — `canonicalise()` hashes a BODY and does not know which chain it belongs to**, so partitioning does not reopen G20 and nothing here suggests it does. > 🛑 **G167–G178 ARE THE TWELVE RULINGS RECORDED IN NO ADJUDICATION, AND MINTING
> THEIR NUMBERS IS AN ACT THIS PLACEMENT TOOK DELIBERATELY.**
> `docs/build/owner-rulings-10-aug.md` §4.6 records that its author would not mint
> them — *"minting twelve more on my own initiative would be a different act"* —
> and left them at §3.1–§3.12 with no rows anywhere. **They are numbered here, in
> the order that document records them being taken, which is the same convention
> §1's allocation used.** The rulings themselves are the owner's; **only the
> numbers are new, and a number is the one thing a later reader can safely
> renumber if the owner disagrees.**

| | Decision | Consequence | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| G167 | cross-track — **D1's TENANT SELECTION INCLUDES BOTH SESSION ARMS** (S-21) | `selectTenantForSession()` returns a **reasoned union** and accepts **EITHER** a `Membership` (`model/domain.ts:1440`) — the customer arm — **or** a live `TenantAccessGrant` (`model/governance.ts:854`) — the staff arm — with the resource class checked against **ALL THREE constants, not two**: `PERMITTED_RESOURCES` (`model/governance.ts:432`), `CONTRACT_ONLY_RESOURCES` (`:512`) and `NON_DELEGABLE_RESOURCES` (`:544`). **Why all three, and it is not belt-and-braces:** invariant 8 records that **G75 existed because a third list nobody had named made a whole ruling inert**, and `authorisationPermits()` (`model/governance.ts:697`) tests `NON_DELEGABLE_RESOURCES` **first, before the withdrawal check.** A picker consulting two of the three reproduces G60's defect exactly. **Why it was necessary:** a picker built only on `Membership` is **EMPTY for a platform FDE**, so `Session.tenantId` could never be set for staff and **invariant 8's permitted path would be structurally unreachable.** Cost accepted: **D1 grows — the session surface now contains grant checking, which is access-model logic rather than session logic.** The staging alternative is preserved: *"excluding it is defensible staging ONLY if D1 says so out loud"* — **the owner declined the staging option rather than taking it silently.** 🛑 The three-list check must be **one helper with one call site**, never three inline `includes()` — a second implementation of the order is §5.3, and **the order is load-bearing.** ⚠️ `grep -rl selectTenantForSession model/*.ts` → 0 files | not applied |
| G168 | ingestion — **v1 BUILDS THE CORRECTION / RE-PARSE PATH** (O-20) | ⚠️ **A FRAMING DISCREPANCY IS RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN RESOLVED, AND THIS ROW DELIBERATELY DOES NOT ASSERT THE AGAINST-ADVICE FRAMING.** The ruling was handed over as *"chosen against the written recommendation"*, with the rejected advice given as *"enumerable now, fixable later"* — **that phrase appears verbatim nowhere in the tree**, and the written recommendation was **not against building**: it reads *"YES for mappings, NO for anything else … but it is a scope decision with a G number, not a derivation."* **What the adjudicator refused was green presenting it as a derivation.** The owner's choice supplies exactly what was missing. **The NO-branch advice is preserved verbatim anyway, because it is the argument a later reader will use to reopen this:** *"`MAPPING_RETRACTION_UNMAKES_DOWNSTREAM = false` is the whole answer, a wrong mapping is undone by hand, and C8's `mappingVersionId` makes the blast radius enumerable without making it fixable."* **Cost accepted, in two parts. (a) It un-drops a family:** six `@dropped-for-v1` markers in `model/learning.ts` carry one note verbatim (`grep -c 'retraction is unbuilt in v1' model/learning.ts` → 6), at `:1188`, `:1206`, `:1222`, `:1239`, `:1248`, `:1285`. **Building the mapping analogue makes this asymmetric ON PURPOSE — mappings get correction, learning does not — and the asymmetry must be written on BOTH sides or the next reader reads the learning drop as an oversight. (b) It cannot be an in-place edit**, and the ground is mechanical: **only two streams in the model are hash-chained, so an in-place recapture leaves every chain valid and every anchor matching while silently changing what every recorded finding means.** 🟢 Verified: `model/domain.ts:3939`, `model/governance.ts:1158`. **The shape must be a COMPENSATING act.** ⚠️ Needs `mappingVersionId` (`grep -rl mappingVersionId model/*.ts` → 0 files), an append-only capture ledger, a plan, a per-document gate, **and a fourteenth `RetentionClass` — which collides with G158's** | not applied |
| G169 | ingestion — **A CORRECTION OF OUR OWN ERROR IS NEVER METERED** (O-21) | **The premise, verified: `Exception.carriedForwardFrom` already exists for exactly this** — ⚠️ **cited as `model/domain.ts:2952` with its docblock at `:2946-2951` until 19 Sep 2026, and BOTH still resolved: `:2952` is a bare `}`. THE DECLARATION IS 1,792 LINES FURTHER DOWN. This is the resolving-but-wrong class landing on THE VERIFIED PREMISE OF A RULING, which is the worst place it can land — a reader checking the premise would have found a closing brace and concluded the row invented its own evidence. Derive it, and the number is deliberately not restated: `grep -n 'carriedForwardFrom' model/*.ts` returns exactly ONE line, which is still the whole finding** — and its docblock says so — *"Also stops the billable `exceptions_raised` meter inflating on every re-run."* `exceptions_raised` is a real summed billable meter (derive it: `grep -n "exceptions_raised" model/billing.ts` — the key and its `'sum'` aggregation; ⚠️ **cited as `:81` and `:103` until 19 Sep 2026 and both had drifted by one and seven lines respectively, which is the cheap end of the same class**). 🛑 **Nothing sets the field and no post-condition checks it — `grep -n 'carriedForwardFrom' model/*.ts` returns ONE line, the declaration. So today a 40,000-document correction of our own bad mapping bills the customer for it, and the field that exists to prevent that is inert.** RULED: the field is **set on every derived exception** **AND** **a post-condition asserts it**, so the meter cannot inflate even if a caller forgets — because *"a rule keyed on a convenient landmark instead of the property it protects is the most common defect in this codebase"*, and a field whose correctness depends on every future caller remembering it is that shape. ⚠️ **Cost accepted, and it is a design constraint rather than a price: *"our own error"* must be a RECORDED FACT on the correction, never a judgement made at billing time.** If billing infers it, the distinction is **unauditable and disputable** — a customer who believes a re-run was our fault has nothing to point at, and neither do we. ⚠️ **Recommendation, explicitly NOT part of the ruling:** make it an arm of the correction's own cause type. **The owner ruled THAT the fact must be recorded, not WHERE** | not applied |

THE VALUE 900 IS STILL CORRECT; the citations were not. Derive: `grep -n 'export const MAX_AUTHORIZATION_SECONDS\|export function authorize' model/access.ts`.** **A node death plus a requeue can resume long after 900 seconds, so G121's one-grant-per-map cannot span a resume.** Nothing in the model is wrong; the grant simply expires. RULED: each resume **authorises itself afresh** and **records the grant it continues.** 🛑 **The condition the owner accepted is the whole safety of the ruling: THE MINT MUST RE-CHECK WITHDRAWAL.** Without it an automatic retry **re-mints an authority a human revoked** — the retry becomes a mechanism for undoing a revocation, **strictly worse than the expiry it was meant to survive.** **Also ruled, as an omission rather than a choice:** the executor calls `redeemAuthorization()` (derive: `grep -n 'export function redeemAuthorization' model/access.ts`; ⚠️ **cited as `:1753` until 19 Sep 2026 and resolving to something else**) **on every attempt**, so an expired grant is refused rather than assumed live — the model already argues for it at `model/access.ts`'s *"A REFERENCE, NOT A BEARER TOKEN"* declaration, *"A REFERENCE, NOT A BEARER TOKEN."* Cost accepted: **one authorisation round-trip per attempt instead of per run**, and a chain field. 🛑 **G121's *"one `AuthorizationGrant` per map execution"* is NARROWED to one per attempt, so the G121 row must be amended rather than merely cited.** ⚠️ `authorize()` mints and nothing else does (invariant 10) — **a second minting path would break invariant 10 outright** | not applied |

The owner took zero, and that is preserved because the weaker form will look like a reasonable simplification to somebody later, and it is not: a map retry bounded below `maxAttempts` still multiplies, just by a smaller factor.** Cost accepted, plainly: **Step Functions' built-in backoff and jitter are given up and must be implemented in the queue** — real work, and then **visible in a table rather than in a state-machine definition**, which is a durable gain. ⚠️ `NormalisationReader` is a **synchronous** function type (`model/reconciliation.ts:2590`) and the stub beside it returns a REFUSAL rather than a fabricated value; **the pre-read must refuse in that same shape, never return an empty outcome** | not applied |

Nothing under `server/` writes a URL literal. 🛑 **TWO CONSEQUENCES THAT ARE SECURITY PROPERTIES RATHER THAN STYLE.** ajv **REJECTS rather than strips** (`removeAdditional: false`, `server/http/app.ts:119`): under Fastify's default `?tenantId=ten_globex` is **SILENTLY DELETED and the request is served**, which satisfies invariant 1 and leaves no evidence that it did. And **authentication runs in `onRequest`, BEFORE validation** (`:125-139`), so a malformed unauthenticated request gets `401` and not `400` — *a validator that answers before an authenticator is a schema oracle.* 🟢 **`GET /v1/runs` CARRIES NO TENANT PREDICATE** — no `WHERE tenant_id = $1`, nothing a reviewer must remember; isolation is produced entirely by the RLS policy reached through `withTenantScope()`, and the handler opens no transaction of its own because `SET LOCAL` outside a transaction block is silently discarded. **THREE DEPENDENCIES, PINNED EXACT** — `fastify@5.12.5` (⚠️ **this row said `5.12.0` until 19 Sep 2026, and the bump is not housekeeping: GHSA-w2qp-rph6-63g4 is a SCHEMA VALIDATION BYPASS via root primitive coercion mismatch, which lands squarely on the sentence this row is about — the contracts ARE the validator — and GHSA-3m5p-2c4r-xxw2 is `X-Forwarded-*` spoofing under `trustProxy` hop-count**), `pg@8.23.0`, `yaml@2.9.0`; derive with `node -e "console.log(require('./package.json').dependencies)"`. 🟢 **G109 IS APPLIED FOR THE FIRST TIME** — a real YAML parser, pinned exact, at `server/contract/document.ts:30`, because the ruling says do not hand-roll one; nothing in `server/` scans a line of YAML. ⚠️ **The line scanners in `tools/` and `tests/` are untouched, and `tests/http/plane-separation.test.ts:33-35` still says G109's parser is *"ruled and unbought"* — false since `ed41d31b`, and not this row's to edit.** ⚠️ **A G98 DEVIATION, FLAGGED RATHER THAN ABSORBED:** `pg` lands in **`dependencies`**, not the `devDependencies` slot G98's row names. Suspending a tenant does not stop it. Nothing stops it but time."* **A membership change stops nothing. A tenant suspension stops nothing.** That is the entire reason the lifetime is minutes rather than a working day, and the entire reason the fence is a flag rather than a key. 🟢 **THE TOKEN IS THE SESSION** — the only reading under which a token that CARRIES a tenant satisfies invariant 1, *"tenant scope is derived from the session, never read from a request."* It is signed HMAC-SHA256 server-side, **verified server-side**, and the tenant is read from the **VERIFIED payload and from nowhere else**; a header or query parameter naming a tenant is the direct inversion and stays refused — visibly, because of G191's `removeAdditional: false`. 🟢 **MINTING IS ALWAYS ALLOWED AND ONLY ACCEPTANCE IS GATED**, and the asymmetry is load-bearing rather than lazy: the assertion that matters is that a **perfectly valid, correctly signed** token is refused by a plane started without the flag, **and a minter that checked the flag could not produce the token that assertion needs.** 🛑 **THE FLAG IS THE BOUNDARY AND THE SIGNING KEY IS A PUBLISHED CONSTANT, DELIBERATELY** (`PUBLISHED_DEV_KEY`, `server/dev/test-token.ts:124`; overridable and unset everywhere). A secret default would suggest the **key** is the control and invite *"we rotated it"* as one; the flag's **absence** from an image and a task definition is a thing an auditor can read. ⚠️ **THAT ARGUMENT HAS A SECOND HALF AND IT WAS MISSING FOR ONE COMMIT, WHICH IS WHY IT IS RECORDED HERE:** it holds only while whoever holds the key cannot **reach** a flag-on process, and `compose.yaml` published both planes on every interface until **G193**'s commit bound them to loopback. **The consequence was verified live rather than reasoned about** — a self-minted token for `ten_globex` was accepted and returned all four of that tenant's runs, and the control plane needed no credential at all. **WHAT MOVED OUT OF THE MINTER AND INTO THE VERIFIER, because the minter is the half an attacker does not run:** `exp - iat > 3600` is refused (the default stays 300); **`iat` is REQUIRED**, because its absence is the one-character bypass of the line above; an `iat` more than 60s in the future is refused, the arithmetic bypass — **60 rather than 0 because a container's clock disagrees with its host's, and a control that fails while the property holds is a control people switch off**; and the tenant id must match `/^ten_[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9_]{0,60})$/`, which is **G97's mint-time rule finally acquiring a mint-time enforcement point on this path** — ` ten_acme`, `ten_ACME`, `*`, `%`, a quote, a newline and a 5,000-character id all reached `withTenantScope()` and became the RLS predicate. **Every verification failure returns the same `null`**, so no caller can treat a class as recoverable and no attacker can distinguish the classes from outside. 🛑 **AND THE SAME FLAG MEANT TWO DIFFERENT THINGS ON THE TWO PLANES, WHICH IS §5.1 ARRIVING INSIDE THE FENCE.** `resolveChannelReader()` returned a principal **without looking at the request**: `GET /catalogue/packs` returned 200 and the full pack list with no credential, and again with a garbage `Authorization` header — while both files' comments called it *"the same flag, read the same way."* The flag was identical; the thing on the far side of it was not. Both planes now verify the same signed credential through the same dynamic import, so **a plane without the flag never loads the accepting module**, and 🛑 **the tenant claim is DISCARDED at the control-plane seam** — invariant 3 — with the test asserting the consequence rather than the intent: two sessions naming two different tenants must receive **byte-identical** catalogues | 🟠 **applied in `server/dev/`, `server/*/start.ts` and `tests/http/` ONLY.** `model/access.ts`'s *"A REFERENCE, NOT A BEARER TOKEN"* declaration is unchanged **and must stay so**. 🛑 **G143 and G149 are NOT amended by this row and their sentences stand** — a later reader finding this table permitting a signed token **in the request path** has read it wrong. ⚠️ **#216 IS STILL OPEN AND ITS FENCE IS NOT THE FENCE THAT LANDED:** its acceptance criteria require a secret with **no default** and a process that **refuses to start** without one; the built form refuses that shape on the argument above. **The issue's checklist and the tree disagree, and the tree is what runs.** ⚠️ **DEMOLITION IS REMEMBERED, NOT MECHANISED:** #157 is to delete this when `Session` lands, and **nothing fails if it does not** |

It is refused on arithmetic rather than taste: **a conflicting PR against a record that takes four rulings in a day is refreshed into a tree that has already moved**, so the work is spent twice and the second spend is not smaller than the first. ⚠️ **The cost of taking it is real and is stated: a closed PR is materially less likely to be revived than a stale one**, and some of these carry reasoning that exists nowhere else — **#175's seven rows are the clearest case**, since they are rulings, and a ruling with no row is *"a ruling the next person mints over"*, which this record has watched happen twice. **The close comment is what makes that survivable, which is why it is the ruling and not the etiquette** | `not applied` — **and it is the one row in this pass that no commit can ever apply**, because it governs a queue rather than a tree. `ls tools/*.mjs` returns **5** checkers and **not one of them can see a pull request**; `npm run check` is EXIT-unchanged by every triage decision this ruling licenses. 🛑 **NO PR IS CLOSED BY THIS COMMIT.** The row places the ruling; the triage is a separate act with a separate audit trail, and folding them together would put "why this was closed" in a commit message rather than on the PR where the person who opened it will look. ⚠️ **The candidates named above are OBSERVATIONS, not a close list** — #114, #133, #178/#183 and #181/#184 are the ones the derivation surfaces, and **which of each pair survives is not this row's to decide** |

| G229 | identity — **AN INVITATION IS REDEEMED, NOT MINTED. ### 3c. The 8 August 2026 verifications — what the vendor documentation actually says

> **The first time this record checked a vendor claim against the vendor's own
> documentation rather than reasoning about it.** Two verifications were run,
> both of which `docs/HANDOFF.md` had carried as open items *"checkable in an
> afternoon"* for a day. **Both changed a decision.** That is the argument for
> doing this before a decision rather than after, and it is why G53, G57, G62,
> G68 and G69 all carry amendments dated 8 Aug.

**Verification 1 — Amazon Textract language coverage.** Carried as a ⚠️ on G53
and amended by G69; now settled by G85.

| Claim | Finding |
|---|---|
| Printed text | English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese **only** |
| Handwriting | *"the Standard English alphabet and ASCII symbols"* **only** |
| CJK / Mandarin | **None, in either mode.** Not mentioned anywhere in the service documentation |
| `ap-southeast-1` | ✅ available since October 2019 |

Source: [Amazon Textract FAQs](https://aws.amazon.com/textract/faqs/) ·
[Textract in Singapore](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2019/10/amazon-textract-is-now-available-in-the-asia-pacific-singapore-region/).

**Verification 2 — Amazon Quick Suite.** Carried as a ⚠️ on G57 and G70.

| Claim | Finding |
|---|---|
| Quick Suite in `ap-southeast-1` | ⚠️ **Subset only.** The Region table marks Singapore `*`, and the note reads *"\*Only Quick Sight features are supported in these regions."* Full Suite is in `us-east-1`, `us-west-2`, `ap-southeast-2`, `ap-northeast-1`, `eu-central-1`, `eu-west-1`, `eu-west-2` → **G82** |
| Q in Quick inference | ⚠️ *"your input prompts and output results may move outside of your primary Region"*, and *"CloudWatch and CloudTrail logs won't specify the AWS Region in which data inference occurs."* Singapore routes across seven Regions; Sydney across two → **G83** |
| RLS owner bypass | ⚠️ *"When you share a dataset with RLS with dataset owners, they can still see all the data."* → **G84** |
| RLS field types | 🛑 *"Row-level security works only for fields containing textual data… It doesn't currently work for dates or numeric fields."* → **§4.1, the `valueCeiling` finding** |
| Namespaces as a tenant boundary | 🟢 **They are not one, which VINDICATES G70.** *"Amazon Quick assets and resources, including datasets, data sources, dashboards, analyses, and so on, exist outside of any namespace"*, and in the admin console *"only IAM permissions are enforced. Users operate outside of the namespace context."* Namespace-per-tenant would not have isolated tenant data; account-per-tenant does |
| Namespace constraints | Custom namespaces require **IAM federated SSO** — no IAM Identity Center, no password login, no AD. Constrains pass D's federation work (§9). Supported in `ap-southeast-1`; not in `af-south-1`, `ap-southeast-3`, `ap-southeast-5`, `eu-south-1`, `eu-central-2` |
| RLS failure direction | 🟢 Fails closed: *"If you don't add a rule for a user or group, that user or group can't see any of the data"*, and Quick *"skips empty RLS rules that grant access to everyone."* Matches `DENY_ALL`. Limits: 999 rules per user; 192,000 filter values per restricted field in SPICE |

Sources: [Quick Suite Regions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quicksight/latest/user/regions-aqs.html) ·
[namespaces](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quicksuite/latest/userguide/namespaces.html) ·
[row-level security](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quick/latest/userguide/row-level-security.html) ·
[user-based RLS rules](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quick/latest/userguide/restrict-access-to-a-data-set-using-row-level-security.html) ·
[sharing datasets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quicksight/latest/user/sharing-data-sets.html).

⚠️ **These are dated readings of a moving target.** Every one is a vendor page
that can change without notice, and E4 in §4.4 records exactly this lesson about
licences — *"the licensing work showed how quietly such assumptions expire."*
**Re-verify before each becomes a contractual commitment**, not once.

### 3b. G56's four contradictions with the record — and what settled each

**G56 named four and this section did not exist until the red team reported it
missing (RD-13, 7 Aug 2026).** All four were in fact settled the same evening; the
pointer was written before the answers were.

| # | G56 says | The record said | Settled by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | data sources arrive **in different currencies** | `docs/v1-scope-ledger.md` §10 item 6: **"One currency"**, with `FxConversion` and `FxPolicy` both dropped | **G61** — display-only, no conversion in matching or ceilings, plus a rate-stamped consolidated total whose rate the customer enters per period |
| 2 | **the FDE configures the sources** | the screen pack puts **Connections and Sources in Tier 3** — customer administrators, rarely | **G59** — FDE-only; they come off the customer surface. ⚠️ Which then collided with invariant 8 and produced **G60** |
| 3 | finance decides which reconciliations run and **"it is not a fixed set"** | the trim had dropped Tier 2 Save entirely — *"every Save button is hidden or greyed with a reason"* | **G58** — finance authors in full. ⚠️ **Now blocked by RD-2**: there is no palette to author with |
| 4 | **submitting documents for compliance** is a third outcome | no screen, no model type, no operation, and no mention anywhere in the record before 7 Aug | **G64** — v1+1, named now so the posting path does not exclude it |

### 3a. G48's consequences — what a product reading changes, and what it does not

**Two drops stop being acceptable and both trace to one missing artefact.**

- ⚠️ **Tier 2 cannot ship read-only.** `docs/v1-scope-ledger.md` §10 item 5 records
  that *"customers cannot save on Reconciliations or Document Types; every Save
  button is hidden or greyed with a reason."* Tier 2 is, in the screen pack's own
  words, **the firm's business logic — owned by finance, versioned, audited,
  changed monthly**. A demo can show a greyed Save. **A product whose central
  premise is that a tolerance is a signed judgement cannot ship without one.** This
  is not primarily a scope choice: it is the missing `administration.openapi.yaml`
  surfacing as a product defect. That file moves from *top of the list* (§8) to
  **the thing v1 is blocked on**.
- ⚠️ **The partner go-to-market is on a spreadsheet.** §10 item 4 accepts *"no
  partner portal and no partner login — **zero drawn screens lost**"*. Zero screens
  is the demo test passing. `PRODUCT.md` records the partner-resell motion as
  **confirmed product truth**, and `docs/screen-pack-ledger.md` §6 records that
  **0 of 18 screens mention a partner**. Under a product reading that is the
  go-to-market, not a deferral — and it is **the same hole G28 names** as the
  taxonomy's missing fourth axis.

**Two standing positions now fire, and both were written with a trigger.**

- **CI.** `CLAUDE.md`: *"Add CI when application code lands, or when a second person
  is committing — not before."* §8 item 8 already argued for the first exception —
  invariant 6 has **one enforcement running instead of two**, and both pack-
  publication validators need a call site. A product ships packs.
- **Counsel moves onto the critical path.** §8 item 2 records that the thirteen
  retention windows and the per-jurisdiction statutory floor map are *"a counsel
  question, not an engineering one — raise it before writing the table, not
  after."* A product stores a real customer's records under a real regime. **This
  now blocks the schema**, which is otherwise unblocked.

**Two decisions were taken on a premise that just moved. NEITHER IS REVERSED HERE**
— §3 says do not relitigate; challenge in writing, with the quote. Both are the
owner's to re-open:

- **G36 (BYOA slips to v1+1).** Its own text says pass F made BYOA a v1 target
  because *"the first non-demo customer is a regulated enterprise, sold direct —
  that reasoning still stands; what changed is that ASAP was not a constraint when
  it was taken."* **G36 traded a reasoning it acknowledged was still true against
  speed.** A product reading raises the price of that trade. It does not settle it,
  because speed may still be the binding constraint.
- **G41 (build the support pop-out, skip the consent record).** Taken against the
  recommendation, knowingly, shipping *"the mechanism without the assurance."*
  `Support.dc.html`'s own sentence is the test: *"an app that can silently ship
  screenshots to a third party fails procurement."* For a demo that is a future
  problem. For a product sold to a regulated enterprise it is a **procurement
  blocker**, and G41 is **already blocked on P10** regardless.

**What does NOT change, and this is the part most easily got wrong.** `PRODUCT.md`
and `CLAUDE.md` forbid claiming a named customer, logo, testimonial, price, SLA or
benchmark, and forbid presenting in-product figures as customer results. **Every
one of those still stands**, because none of them was ever a statement about the
build target — they are statements about evidence we do not have. G48 changes what
we are building. It changes nothing about what may be said.

---

**On G22, because it overrides the design record rather than extending it.**

Mechanically supported: `PERMITTED_RESOURCES.delivery` includes `configuration`
(`model/governance.ts:397`), so an FDE under a delivery grant reaches it today. No
new capability, no class change.

But `Mockups/rec/Setup.dc.html` tags the card `tier: 'Definitions · versioned'` and
its body reads *"the confidence below which a person is asked instead of guessed at.
**The finance half of capture.**"* `Sitemap.dc.html`'s spine states *"Capture splits
across two tiers — what to extract is finance's decision, where files land is not"*,
and the confidence floor is the sole reason that split exists. The pack also answers
the obvious objection: *"Lowering a floor is the fastest way to put a wrong number in
the ledger, so the change is versioned and shows how many of last month's dockets it
would have auto-accepted"* — a preview that converts a tuning number into a finance
judgement.

The owner was shown all three and reaffirmed. **Three consequences follow and none is
solved:**

1. `Setup.dc.html`'s Document types card and `DocumentTypes.dc.html`'s per-field
   floors come off the customer surface, and the Sitemap's capture-split sentence
   becomes false and needs redrawing.
2. **The model has no way to express "configuration the tenant does not see."**
   Resource class carries no visibility term. The only disclosure device is
   `TenantAccessGrant.visibleToTenant` (`model/governance.ts:703`), and `:1270`
   describes hiding in the other direction as *discouraged*. A customer-invisible
   configuration field is a new pattern in a model whose posture is that the tenant
   is told what was done to them. **This is an open engineering question, not a
   settled one.**
3. A 90-day delivery grant can therefore change a threshold that decides whether a
   human checks a number, in a tenant that cannot see the value or its change.
