## 4. Open items, grouped by who can close them

### 4.1 Engineering — ours, no external dependency

**Two findings produced BY the work of 7 Aug, not by a review of it.** Both surfaced
because a compile-time proof rejected something, which is the only reason either is
known.

- **`Timestamp = string` in `model/kernel.ts` is a naked alias.** Same defect class
  slice 4 fixed for `RoleId`, `PolicyId`, `ScorerId` and `AutonomyProposalId`: a
  field typed `Timestamp` reads as checked and accepts any string in the program.
  ⚠️ **It cannot be excepted by any assertion of G47's shape**, because `Timestamp`
  *is* `string` — the compiler cannot distinguish a machine-generated instant from a
  pasted paragraph, and neither can `NoPlainText`. Found when
  `_CarriedTurnHoldsNoText` rejected `CarriedTurn.askedAt`; the field was dropped
  (turn order is positional) rather than the assertion weakened. Branding it is a
  sweep with its own call-site audit and it makes every future no-text proof
  stronger.

- **`entity_without_identity` reads 47 where G35's classification names 40.**
  ⚠️ **This entry said 42 when it was written on 7 Aug and 42 was never the
  reading** — the committed graph said 45 at the time and 42 was
  `entity_unreferenced`, the gap kind directly above it in the extractor's own
  output. Corrected here rather than silently, because a count in prose believed
  instead of derived is §5.11, and this instance appeared in the section that
  catalogues it. **Derive it:** `node tools/planner/extract.mjs`, gap kind
  `entity_without_identity`; it equals the summary's `value objects` line.
  The seven beyond G35's snapshot are `CarriedReading` and `CarriedTurn` (G47),
  `PackBinding` and `TokenUsage` (branded 7 Aug — and note *why* they are here:
  they were the two fields no tool could see, because neither was id-shaped),
  `ProcedureEdge` and `ProcedureViolation` (the slice-6 sweep branded `stepId`,
  `from` and `to`, so they carry branded references for the first time), and
  `ProposedTransaction` (G42). **The sweep surfacing new candidates is the sweep
  working**, not a defect. None of the seven has been classified, and none should
  be folded into the 40 without someone deciding. `docs/identity-classification.md`
  is a dated snapshot against `156ababf` and says so.

**⚠️ NEW 8 Aug 2026 — `AssignmentScope.valueCeiling` is UNENFORCEABLE in the BI
layer, and it is E2's shape recurring inside a bought tool.**

The Quick Suite verification (§3c) found, verbatim: *"Row-level security works
only for fields containing textual data (string, char, varchar, and so on). It
doesn't currently work for dates or numeric fields."*

Two of the six `AssignmentScope` dimensions survive that constraint —
`costCentre` and `legalEntity` are opaque customer strings and express as RLS
rules cleanly. **`valueCeiling` is a monetary amount and has no RLS expression at
all.** So a role narrowed to SGD 5,000 resolves correctly in `model/`, renders
correctly in an access review, and **matches every row in the BI layer**.

**That is exactly E2**, which this record closed on 7 Aug for the opposite
reason: *"A role scoped to two cost centres was, on the exception queue,
unscoped — and it typechecked, read correctly in an access review, and did
nothing."* E2 was a missing column; this is a tool that cannot filter on the
column even when present. **The failure mode and the invisibility are identical.**

⚠️ **No option in the 8 Aug rulings avoids it.** G84's authors-never-owners
closes the *owner bypass*; it does nothing about which field types RLS can
filter on. The only shape that would have was keeping our own scope spine for
the dimensions RLS cannot express — offered, and not taken. **Record what this
means plainly: in v1 the BI layer enforces two of six scope dimensions, and
nothing in `model/` will tell you that.**

> 🛑 **RULED 8 Aug 2026 — G94. G68 STANDS AND THIS COST IS ACCEPTED.**
> `docs/build/phase-one-plan.md` §5 flagged the reopen as the owner's call, with
> **three independent sources converging on it** — RD-3, RD-7 and green-BI
> slice 5 — and §5.8 records convergence as *without exception* the signal worth
> acting on here. **The reopen was put in front of the owner with that fact
> stated and was not taken.** Two alternatives were offered and declined:
> restoring the scope spine from `presentation.ts` for the dimensions RLS cannot
> express, and narrowing what the v1 BI layer shows so `valueCeiling` never has
> to bind there.
>
> **What that means for anyone building the BI layer, stated once, here:** a role
> narrowed to a value ceiling is **not narrowed in Quick Suite**, and no code
> path in `model/` is wrong — which is precisely why nothing will catch it. If
> the BI layer is later asked to show anything where a value ceiling is the
> control that matters, **this ruling is the thing to reopen**, and it should be
> reopened rather than worked around at the call site.

⚠️ **NEW 9 Aug 2026 — CITATION QUALITY FELL 4.6× IN ONE DAY AND THE GATE STAYED
GREEN THROUGHOUT.** `node tools/check-citations.mjs` reported **38** SUSPECT
citations at the start of 9 Aug and **176** at the end of it. Nothing failed,
because the tool exits 0 on SUSPECT and only DEAD fails the run — and every one of
these citations still RESOLVES, to a real line, which is exactly the blind spot the
tool documents about itself: *"a citation that drifted from one real line to
another real line is invisible here."*

**The cause is not carelessness, it is growth.** `model/reconciliation.ts` gained
§10, `model/access.ts` gained capability 37, `model/learning.ts` gained the rule
evaluator and the sixth scope dimension — and every citation into those files below
an insertion point now names a different line than it did. 54 of the 176 point into
`model/domain.ts` alone.

⚠️ **DO NOT BULK-FIX THESE.** A citation repaired by re-running a line number is a
citation nobody read, and this record has been burned by exactly that before —
`docs/INDEX.md` went stale four times because each repair was somebody re-typing a
number. The honest options are a sweep that READS each one, or anchoring citations
on declaration text rather than line numbers so they cannot drift. **The second is
the real fix and it has never been costed.**

**R-1 costed the second option:** new citations may name a declaration or unique
literal anchor in `file#fragment` form, and the citation gate now refuses an
unresolvable or ambiguous fragment. Existing line citations are deliberately not
rewritten here; their human-adjudicated sweep remains separate work.

⚠️ **THREE limits, and none is incidental.**

⚠️ **The third was found on 8 Aug 2026 and it is the worst of them: THE TOOL IS
BLIND TO THE MARKDOWN-TABLE FORM.** Its matcher requires the number
**immediately before** the noun — the prose form, `N exports` — and **cannot see
the table form**, where the noun sits in one cell and the number in the next:

```
| `export` declarations | **N** | grep -h '^export ' model/*.ts | wc -l |
```

**Both of this file's counts tables are that form: §0's reproduction table and
§2's state table.** The consequence is exact and was verified twice. §0's row
claimed **665** exports with the reproducing command sitting beside it, and had
done since before 7 Aug — wrong when the tree said 675, still wrong when it said
683 — through every green run of this tool. It was corrected by hand on 8 Aug,
**and went stale again the same day** when `SERVICE_NOTICE_KINDS` added four
exports, because a hand correction is not a mechanism. **The two tables this
document most insists you derive from are the two it does not check.**

⚠️ **Deliberately, no number appears in this paragraph.** §5.11's own rule is
*write the verb, not the number* — a narration that pins the current value is a
narration with an expiry date, and this one would expire every time the tree
moves. Widening the matcher to the table form is a small change to
`tools/check-doc-counts.mjs` and is **still not made**; until it is, a green run
says nothing about a counts table.

It checks **numbers only** — it
cannot see a stale claim with no number in it, a wrong `file:line` citation, a
drop note on the wrong declaration, or a contract enum drifted from the model.
And it **cannot tell a stale count from a deliberately historical one**, because
this record narrates its own corrections on purpose (§6). So it classifies rather
than fixes: `STALE` fails the run, `HISTORICAL` is reported and never fails. The
classifier is a heuristic over English and is the only part of the tool that
guesses; everything above it is derived. **Every line currently classified
HISTORICAL has been read and is correct as written** — do not bulk-edit them.

⚠️ **THE COUNT OF THEM IS DELIBERATELY NOT STATED HERE, and that is a §5.11
finding rather than laziness.** This sentence read *"Fourteen lines currently
classify HISTORICAL and all fourteen were read"* until 8 Aug 2026. It is
**self-incrementing**: every narration added to this record that quotes a
superseded number becomes another HISTORICAL line, so a paragraph in the
*counts-discipline* section was itself a count going stale on write — it moved
from fourteen to fifteen to sixteen inside one editing session, twice from
sentences written to explain the first move. **Derive it:**

```bash
node tools/check-doc-counts.mjs | grep '^HISTORICAL'
```

⚠️ **Two of the fourteen were reclassified STALE on 8 Aug by a change that did
not touch them**, and the mechanism is worth knowing before it wastes an hour.
`CLAUDE.md`'s two narrations read *"claiming 665 exports against 675"*, and they
classified HISTORICAL only because the window happened to contain **675, the
then-current derived value** — cue 1 of the classifier's three. The fixtures pass
moved exports to 683, the cue evaporated, and two correct sentences began failing
the run. **They were reworded to carry a retrospective cue instead of a number**
— *"when the tree then said 675"* — which is stable under any future count. **A
narration that pins the current value is a narration with an expiry date;** write
the verb, not the number.

argued in `docs/access-and-agency.md` §11.9–§11.11. None is a bug to be swept;

|---|---|---|
| E1 | ~~**Six of thirteen resource classes have no capability pointing at them**~~ — **PARTLY SETTLED 7 Aug 2026. Two of six remain: `schedule`, `telemetry`.** | Original: nothing names a budget, an invoice, a plan, a schedule or a usage record, so **a tenant admin cannot see what they owe**. Adding a capability is a platform release, and `catalogue` proves an empty class can legitimately be a *statement* rather than a gap. The question is gap-or-statement, per class. **Answered per class:** `metering` and `commercial` were gaps → `view_metering` (35) and `view_commercial` (36), taking `CAPABILITIES` to **thirty-six** and the classes with a capability to **nine of thirteen**; `substrate` joins `catalogue` as a **statement** (a release reaches it, a grant does not, and a capability is the currency of grants); `schedule` stays open because the undecided part is **scope semantics** — an armed schedule must pin a scope where every other capability resolves one — not the verb's name. ⚠️ `telemetry` stays open and is still the live inconsistency: it sits in both `PERMITTED_RESOURCES` entries and is bounded in `MAX_AUTHORIZATION_SECONDS`, so a grant reaches it and `authorize()` can never mint for it (§11.9). It is now at least flagged at the class in `model/governance.ts`, which it was not. Full argument: `docs/access-and-agency.md` §11.9a |
| ~~E2~~ | ~~**Two of six scope dimensions bind on nothing**~~ **Applied 7 Aug 2026** | `Exception` carried no cost centre and no legal entity, and neither field existed on any entity in the model. A role scoped to two cost centres was, on the exception queue, unscoped — and it typechecked, read correctly in an access review, and did nothing. **Now:** `TagPolicy.legalEntityKey`, `Exception.costCentre`, `Exception.legalEntity`, and both columns on `Exception` and `ExceptionQueueRow` in `capability.openapi.yaml`. ⚠️ **Representable, not enforced** — nothing reads either column, the resolver from `TagPolicy` does not exist, and the null-excludes rule is carried by SQL's `NULL IN (…)` semantics rather than by any function. Taken now because after the queue exists it is a backfill whose values are guesses about who was allowed to see what (§11.10) |
| E3 | **One capability does install, upgrade *and* disable** | `SOLUTION_CONTAINER_CAPABILITY` maps all three acts to `install_pack` (`model/access.ts:2008`), so **switching off a live reconciliation costs what installing one costs**. Left as one verb deliberately — *"disable feels like it should be separate"* is not an argument that earns a capability number (§11.11) |
| E4 | **No canonicalisation scheme exists for any hash in the repository** | `UsageAttestation.bodyHash` says *"canonical body"* and nothing defines canonical — no JCS, no RFC 8785 — and `RecordChain` now adds two more hashed streams on that base. One document, two parsers, two answers: the CVE-2017-12635 shape. **Pick one before the first hash is computed**; afterwards every stored chain is bound to it (`model/governance.ts:899`) |
| E5 | **Model identities skip `resolveModel()`** — ⚠️ **NARROWED 7 Aug 2026, NOT CLOSED. Four branded, three still bare.** | `resolveModel()` (`model/catalog.ts:184`) is the **only executable enforcement of residency** in the codebase and rejects `global.*` routing unconditionally, so a bare string is a field that reaches a model without passing it. **Branded to `ModelCatalogEntryId` on 7 Aug:** `PackBinding.modelOverride` (`domain.ts:2142`), `TokenUsage.model` (`domain.ts:2491`), `ProposalActor` agent `.modelId` (`domain.ts:3194`), `AuditActor` agent `.modelId` (`governance.ts:964`). **Still bare, and this is the live list:** `UsageRecord.model` (`billing.ts:238` — **live, not dropped**, and it is invariant 5's own record), `PolicySubject` `model_call.model` (`policy.ts:852` — **live**, and invisible to the old grep because it sits inside a union type alias), `Scorer.model` (`evaluation.ts:158` — bare but `@dropped-for-v1`, so consistent with §0). Two more are bare **correctly** under rule R1, because AWS mints the string: `ModelCatalogEntry.modelId` (`catalog.ts:118`) and `resolveModel()`'s own parameter (`catalog.ts:185`). **Reproduce the whole set:** `grep -rnE "\b(model\|modelId\|modelOverride)\s*\??:\s*string\b" model/*.ts \| grep -v '^\S*:[0-9]*: *\*'` → **five** lines, of which two are the R1 pair. **No document may claim the sweep closed E5** — `model/agents.ts:747` shows the fix, and two live fields still skip it |
| E6 | **No `author_harness` verb** | Harness authoring borrows `author_procedure` (`model/agents.ts:514`). Correctly not invented locally — but it means a harness edit and a procedure edit are indistinguishable in an access review |

| E4 | **Mastra licence** — re-verify before committing | Verdict recorded 4 Aug: Apache-2.0 core, `ee/` excluded, builder built by us. Licences change. `docs/integration-options.md` §2.4 |
| E5 | **Can the adjacent-domain engagements be named publicly?** (KYC, credit underwriting, medical records) | Client permission. `PRODUCT.md` |

### 4.5 Accepted risks — recorded, not resolved

| # | Item |
|---|---|
| K1 | **Live IAM key** `AKIAXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX` in `sap_erp_website_lambda`, invoked by an unauthenticated public form. Deferred by product-owner decision 4 Aug. **`docs/infrastructure-risk-register.md` §1** — the finding moved there on 6 Aug when `docs/compliance-checklist.md` left the trunk, because it is a property of AWS account `000000000000`, which the rebuild inherits, and not of the deleted code. The original text is at `archive/design-record:docs/compliance-checklist.md` §6 (Addendum — Secrets Management) |
| K2 | **PITR window versus erasure** — a 35-day window means a deleted subject stays recoverable for 35 days |
| K3 | **Traces exported to a customer's own endpoint cannot be deleted by us.** `TelemetryExport.acknowledgedTransfer` makes it disclosed, not solved |

## 5. What reviews found that types could not

**This is the most useful section in the file.** Fourteen review agents ran on
5 Aug: three layer reviews (one per contract), five vertical-slice reviews tracing
API-to-model, four on hierarchy and agent principals, one coverage pass, and one
red team on `model/access.ts`. The model typechecked clean before every one of
them and after every one of them. Everything below was invisible to the compiler.

The findings fall into recurring shapes. **Learn the shapes; they will recur** —
and they did. **§5.10 and §5.11 were added 7 Aug 2026** from the v1 sequence,
which was five steps of type-level work with a green `tsc` throughout, and which
produced two shapes the 5 Aug reviews had not seen. That is the strongest evidence
this section is worth maintaining: the shapes recurred in a different kind of work,
against a different set of files, within two days.

**Nine shapes, §5.1–§5.7 plus §5.10–§5.11.** §5.8 and §5.9 are meta-findings about
how to review, not defects.

### 5.1 A rule keyed on a convenient landmark instead of the property it cares about

The most common defect, and it found itself twice in one afternoon, one node
apart.

- `validateProcedureInjectionSafety()` **derived entry points from `await`
  steps.** Admission does not require an `await` — a procedure of
  `agent(admit) → agent(propose) → notify` produced *zero* entry points and passed
  the gate clean. Entries are now `await`-on-reply **or** any agent step whose
  action is `admit`. `model/domain.ts:657`, fixed in `8b0b015e`.
- The same rule's human-step condition keyed on **step kind**. A `human` step of
  any sort laundered an untrusted path, which made the control satisfiable with a
  rubber stamp. It now requires `correspondence` in `requiredEvidence`.

The tell: a rule whose predicate names a *structure* (`await`, `human`) when the
property it protects is a *behaviour* (admits untrusted content, actually reads
it). The structure is easier to find in the graph, which is exactly why it gets
written.

### 5.2 A caller-supplied parameter that switches a check off

- `validateProcedureInjectionSafety()` took the admitting step ids as a
  **caller-supplied parameter**. Passing an empty array switched off the
  tool-scope half of the trifecta gate — and the caller with the strongest motive
  to pass one is the caller authoring a procedure whose admitting agent carries
  tools. Half the rule was derived from the graph and half was declared; the
  declared half was decorative. Now derived, with nothing to omit. `e54880f3`.
- `assignmentGrants()` answered the capability half of an authorisation question
  and **handed the scope half back to the caller**, in a module where every other
  single-point-of-truth check is a function precisely because a call site
  reasoning independently is the vulnerability. The failure it invited was exact:
  union capabilities and union scopes across assignments, and one unscoped
  read-only role dissolves every value ceiling in the tenant. `effectiveScopeFor()`
  now unions scopes **only across assignments carrying the requested capability**,
  and travels with the answer. `model/access.ts:1148`, and `Decision` at `:937`; `f2d2707e`.

The tell: an argument that the callee could compute itself. If it could, it must.

### 5.3 Two vocabularies for one concept, diverging

Every instance found so far diverged **within hours** of being duplicated.

- **`ErrorCode`.** The three tier specs were authored the same afternoon. The
  capability spec copied the enum at 27 members while the control-plane spec
  extended it to 40 — two definitions disagreeing by thirteen members, inside a
  document set whose stated premise is one vocabulary. Extracted to
  `docs/contracts/errors.yaml` (88 codes — ⚠️ **it said 71 until 23 Aug 2026 and 87
until 19 Sep 2026**; the sixteen the session tier added are mirrored from
`model/` by exact name, and the eighty-eighth is `capability_not_held`, G200's)
and referenced, never copied. Caught
  only by a mechanical cross-file check. `9006d30f`.
- **`RoleKey` versus `Capability`.** The whole of §15 exists because five enum
  members were doing two jobs — a stakeholder's relationship to the work, and a
  capability in the system — so a KYC reviewer and an AP approver were both
  `approver`. ~~The fourteen unmigrated references are the *same* divergence,
  still live, deliberately.~~ **CLOSED 7 Aug 2026** — the enum is deleted and the
  derived per-site table is `docs/domain-model.md` §15.6. The divergence lasted
  two days after it was named, and **the count recorded for it was wrong in both
  revisions** (fourteen, then fifteen; the live set was six).
- ⚠️ **`Money` versus `MoneyAmount` — found 7 Aug, unfixed.** The two value
  ceilings a proposal must satisfy are **different interfaces in different
  modules**: `AssignmentScope.valueCeiling` is `Money` (currency / amountMinor /
  exponent, `model/domain.ts:360`) and `AutonomyConfig.autoResolveValueCeiling` is
  `MoneyAmount` (`model/policy.ts:148`, no exponent). Any check that must satisfy
  both — which is every check on the operator-proposal path — has to convert, and
  **no function in the model does**. This is §5.7's currency-arithmetic finding
  wearing a different hat: the exponent is exactly the term whose absence makes
  BHD and USD compare wrongly. Surfaced only because `ProposedTransaction.value`
  is the first field that must be compared against both.
- ⚠️ **`CapabilityRequirement` mirrored in two contract files with two money
  schemas.** One model interface (`model/access.ts`), two wire copies:
  `capability.openapi.yaml` uses `Money` **with** an exponent,
  `control-plane.openapi.yaml` uses `MoneyAmount` **without** one. The model field
  is `Money`, so the control-plane copy is arguably already wrong. Nothing will
  notice when they drift — see §5.10 and §7 on the missing checker.
- **`AgentAction` versus `Capability`.** `AgentAction` named `execute_resolution`
  and `close_exception`; neither had a capability. `AutonomyConfig` could permit
  the two acts that change the ledger while the capability layer had no verb to
  gate them with. `6711cf2f`.
- **`AgentAction` had no `admit` at all** — the single most security-critical act
  an agent can take could not be named, so policy could not evaluate it. Three
  `ErrorCode` values in the contract referred to a control no operation could
  invoke, which is what exposed it. **An unnameable action is an ungoverned one.**
  `e54880f3`.
- **The proposer.** `policy.ts` listed `propose_resolution` as an agent action
  while `domain.ts` typed the proposer as a `UserId` — the two contradicted each
  other on the core act of an agentic product. `docs/domain-model.md` §13.4.

The tell: the same noun appearing in two modules with two spellings of its value
set. Grep for the values, not the type name.

### 5.4 A claim asserted in a document that the contracts refute

Tracing prose against a contract is a different exercise from reviewing either.

- **The metering "floor".** See §6.
- **`PolicyEvaluation` "PII-free by construction".** See §6.
- **"Policy authored centrally"** in constraint C2 would have produced the wrong
  build. `Policy` is tenant-scoped, adopted by a tenant admin, and under BYOA
  already sits in the customer's own database with nothing to distribute. C2
  covers platform defaults, templates and the model catalogue. Reading it as *us
  setting a customer's autonomy ceiling remotely* was one sentence away.
  `682b0e3c`.
- **"Distributed"** described the logical direction while the connection is
  always a **pull** by the plane — a push needs inbound access into a customer
  account and no security team grants it. Same commit.
- ⚠️ **The access-path enums named a resource class that had stopped existing.**
  `AccessResourceGrant.resource` and `AccessSessionReport.touched[].resource` in
  `control-plane.openapi.yaml` both enumerated
  `[telemetry, configuration, sample_data, tenant_data]`. `sample_data` was
  removed as a class on 5 Aug (pass E, §11.3) and there are thirteen classes. It
  was **wrong in both directions**: it named a class `grantAllows()` can no longer
  be handed, *and* omitted `identity`, `endpoint` and `authority` — so a plane
  validating against it would have **refused a well-formed `authority` grant**,
  the one class a `SupportAuthorisation` exists to open, while accepting a
  `sample_data` line no function in the model can evaluate. Fixed 7 Aug; the enum
  is now the six values *derived* from `PERMITTED_RESOURCES.delivery ∪
  PERMITTED_RESOURCES.incident ∪ CONTRACT_ONLY_RESOURCES`, not chosen. **It sat
  there for two days and was seen and re-reported by three consecutive workflow
  steps, each of which declined to fix it because closing it *looked* like a
  decision.** It was a transcription. §7 carries the lesson.

### 5.5 Invalid states that the type made legal

- **`ExceptionResolution` was a flat record with independently nullable fields**,
  which made *mode autonomous with no authorising policy* a valid value — the
  exact state it was created to prevent, legal in the type meant to prevent it.
  And manual mode named nobody: `decidedBy` documented the approver, so the person
  who actually acted was recorded nowhere. Now a discriminated union.
  `model/domain.ts:1603`.
- **Scope polarity was inverted and failed OPEN.** Dimensions were `T[] | null`
  with `null` meaning unrestricted, so a freshly constructed scope was maximally
  permissive and every failed resolution degraded *to* it. Every other failure
  path in this codebase fails closed — `grantAllows` treats an empty nomination
  list as granting nothing rather than everything. Scope is now an explicit
  all-or-these union, empty denies, and `DENY_ALL` is the failure value.
  `model/access.ts:512,575,590`.
- **A third `environment` value with no `PackBinding`** — a hole that typechecks
  perfectly and misbehaves at runtime. `bindingFor()` falls back to the production
  binding and never the sandbox one, because falling back to sandbox would run a
  prospect's real data through a cheaper model with autonomy disabled.
  `ce3a44fd`.

### 5.6 Controls that pass while asserting nothing

- **`segregationOfDuties` against an agent proposer.** `approver !== proposer` is
  trivially true against `ProposalActor.agent`. A control that always passes is a
  false assurance, which is worse than a missing one. Flagged, not fixed — §4.1.
- **`ApprovalConfig` had no value gate on the human path.**
  `autoResolveValueCeiling` binds agents only, and `secondApproverAbove` exists
  only if a procedure routes through a human step. So a person could execute
  unbounded value on a low-severity exception with no approval at all — and
  severity is deliberately decoupled from value elsewhere, so
  high-value-implies-high-severity was never available as a defence. `8b0b015e`.
- **A gate present on three paths and absent on the fourth.** Prompt, telemetry
  and outbound all carry a classification ceiling. **Screen does not** — a browser
  reading `explanation.observed[]` passes no ceiling at all. Open as V7.
- **`METER_AGGREGATION` had zero call sites** while existing solely to stop a
  stock meter being summed. `RatedTotal` now carries `aggregation`. `8b0b015e`.

### 5.7 Arithmetic that silently assumes one unit

**Cross-currency ceiling comparison is now refused rather than approximated.** BHD
carries three decimal places and USD two, so equal minor units differ by roughly
3.8×, and a naive comparison accepts a child ceiling four times its parent's.
`model/access.ts:1213,1868`, `f2d2707e`.

### 5.8 Convergence is the signal

Findings that two agents reached independently, from different mandates, were
without exception the ones worth acting on:

- **`ProcedureStepExecution`** — found by the exception-slice review and the
  agency review, from opposite ends of the system.
- **`input_tokens` / `output_tokens` have no producer** — found by three agents
  separately.
- **Agents hold no roles** — two agents with opposing mandates reached the same
  conclusion, and it *reversed* a position stated an hour earlier in the same
  session.
- **Six hierarchies collapse to two mechanisms** — the green team and an
  independent prior arrived at the same collapse.

### 5.9 The meta-finding

The coverage pass produced a percentage that was not useful — a textual check
undercounts, because a contract modelling the same concept under a different
schema name reads as absent when it is not. The **categorical** result was the
finding: every contract written describes a reconciliation *happening*, and
nothing describes setting the system up.

It stayed invisible because **every review so far had followed a reconciliation
through the system.** Nothing had followed a customer through onboarding — except
`docs/user-journeys.html`, which is exactly where the unmodelled steps showed up
first, a day earlier.

> If you are choosing a review to run next: pick a **path nobody has walked**, not
> a layer somebody has already read.

### 5.10 A total record with no construction site — ⚠️ NEW, 7 Aug 2026

**The defect shape this repository is currently most exposed to, and it appeared
five times in five consecutive steps.** It is the reason a green `tsc` is weak
evidence here.

A total `Record<K, V>` over a closed key set is the house pattern (`CLAUDE.md`,
Writing model code) precisely because an unhandled member becomes a compile error.
**But a total record only bites where something CONSTRUCTS one.** In a
types-only model nothing does — so the compiler confirms the *shape* is total and
never confirms that any *content* satisfies it.

The five instances, all landed 7 Aug — ✅ **all five now have a construction
site, 8 Aug 2026**, in `model/examples.ts` under the `FIXTURES` banner:

| Added | Nothing constructed it — until | Witness |
|---|---|---|
| `FieldSpec.confidenceFloor` | no `FieldSpec` object literal existed anywhere in `model/` | `invoiceFieldSpecs` — both arms, a total at `0.95` and a description at `null` |
| `PolicyDefaults` (total over `LivePolicyKind`) | no `PolicyDefaults` value | `PLACEHOLDER_POLICY_DEFAULTS` |
| `RetentionPolicy.days` (total over 13 `RetentionClass`) | no `RetentionPolicy` value | `PLACEHOLDER_RETENTION_POLICY` |
| `CapabilityRequirement` on the wire | nothing constructed one | `fourEyesAboveThreshold` |
| every type in the operator-proposal path | no `OperatorProposal` value | `inventoryReading` → two proposals → `operatorDecisions` |

Each had been defended with a **compile-time assertion** instead
(`_RetentionPolicyAnswersEveryClass`, `_OperatorProposalIsNotExceptionAnchored`,
and so on), each verified RED and reverted. That is genuine and it holds the
shape. It is strictly weaker than a fixture, because an assertion cannot catch a
field whose *value* is wrong, only one whose *type* is.

**The assertions were NOT retired.** A fixture witnesses content; an assertion
states the intent at the declaration, where the next person edits. Retiring one
is a separate decision — `RetentionPolicy`'s own comment invites it (*"Retire it
the day a fixture or a migration constructs a real policy"*) and that invitation
was deliberately not taken here.

**Two red runs, because a fixture claiming to be a witness and never seen failing
is the same defect one level up:**

- A **fourteenth `RetentionClass`** added to `RETENTION_CLASSES` →
  `model/examples.ts(527,3): error TS2741: Property 'red_flag_test_class' is
  missing … but required in type 'Record<RetentionClass, number>'`. Note what
  this proves: `_RetentionPolicyAnswersEveryClass` **cannot** catch this — it is
  `AssertAnswersEveryRetentionClass<RetentionPolicy['days']>`, and
  `Record<RetentionClass, number>` still satisfies `Record<RetentionClass,
  unknown>` however many members `RetentionClass` gains. The assertion catches a
  relaxation to `Partial`; only the fixture catches a new class.
- **`LivePolicyKind` widened to `PolicyKind`** — the exact experiment
  `model/policy.ts` describes — →
  `model/examples.ts(614,14): error TS2739: … missing the following properties
  from type 'PolicyDefaults': spend, content_guardrail`. That file's comment said
  this widening *"produced NO error… The first bundle fixture is what would
  witness it."* It does now.

⚠️ **What the fixtures still do not witness.** Values, not correctness: no number
in them is authoritative, and two are named `PLACEHOLDER_` for that reason —
the thirteen retention windows remain a **counsel** question (§8 item 2) and
nothing here answers it. They also witness nothing about the wire: the
`CapabilityRequirement` fixture is the model side only, and the two contract
copies still carry two different money schemas with nothing watching them (§5.3).

The tell: you added a field or a key and `tsc` stayed green **without you having
to change anything else**. In this repository that is the normal case, and it
means the compiler told you nothing.

### 5.11 A count stated in prose, believed instead of derived — ⚠️ NEW, 7 Aug 2026

Three instances in three days, which makes it the shape rather than three
accidents:

- **"Fourteen `RoleKey` references"**, then fifteen. The live set was **six**, and
  **every line-number citation in the recorded list was wrong**. Nine of the named
  references had migrated two days earlier.
- **"Thirty-four capabilities"**, in `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/access-and-agency.md` and
  `docs/INDEX.md`, after two more were minted.
- **"Forty-three decisions"**, in this file's own §3 header, while G44 was live
  and governing an orchestration brief — a decision that governs work and appears
  in no decision table.

Plus the delta table asserting delta 1 **outstanding** for two days after it had
shipped — which is worse than the others, because that row stood against a
**closed union**, and the fix for an "outstanding" variant is to add one.

The tell: a number written as a word in prose, with no command beside it. **Every
count in this file and in `CLAUDE.md` now carries the command that reproduces it.**
Where you cannot write the command, write the uncertainty instead.

---

## 6. Corrections left visible

Where a document was wrong, the correction stays in the record rather than being
quietly edited. Future readers need to know a file has been wrong before.

**The metering "floor" does not exist, and `data-architecture.md` claimed it did.**
§11.1 built the metering trust model on three layers and called the first a floor
of control-plane-observed events that "cannot be under-reported", sourced from
pack activation, policy fetch and model resolution. Traced against the contracts,
**none of the three is observable by the control plane**: model resolution is an
in-plane foundation service, policy fetch is daily and deliberately
volume-independent (that is the entire point of constraint C1), and pack
activation is the plane reporting its own installations. The layered model was one
mechanism — self-report. §4.1 states the floor-versus-C1 conflict correctly and
§11.1 then re-asserted the floor anyway. The correction is **not** a better floor;
nothing in the design is both proportional to volume and outside the customer's
account. The bound moves *inside* the signed artefact:
`UsageAttestation.drawdownHighWater` (`model/billing.ts:562`) is the lease counter
in the body a KMS key signs. Correction lives at
**`docs/data-architecture.md:480`**.

**`PolicyEvaluation.reason` was cited as a closed vocabulary before it was one.**
`persistence-design.md` §11.5 had it right — it lists *"PII-free by construction,
not by convention — `PolicyEvaluation.reason` drawn from a closed vocabulary"* as
constraint 2 of three, a **condition** for keeping the record movable to another
store. Later documents
restated the condition as a fact — `data-architecture.md` classified
`PolicyEvaluation` as "PII-free by construction", and `day-2-operations.md` said
the closed-vocabulary rule was already applied there. It was not: the field was
`string`, documented as human-readable and shown to the user, which carries tenant
content within a week of shipping. It is now `PolicyReasonCode`, with the human
sentence rendered from it rather than stored beside it. The rule was right; the
citation was not. Corrections live at **`docs/data-architecture.md:460`**,
**`docs/day-2-operations.md:70`**, and in the comment at
**`model/correspondence.ts:132`**.

**`admittingStepIds` was reintroduced into a spec after the model deleted it.**
The parameter was removed from `validateProcedureInjectionSafety()` on 5 Aug
because an empty array switched half the trifecta gate off. The foundation
contract kept it for a few hours longer. It is now recorded as a deliberate
absence, in the request description itself, at
**`docs/contracts/foundation.openapi.yaml:744`** — *"NOTE WHAT IS ABSENT"* — with
a back-reference at **`model/domain.ts:698`**.

Two older corrections still stand and should not be re-broken: `PRODUCT.md` on
the admin gate, and `docs/domain-model.md` §7 on the domain-neutrality claim.

## 7. Traps that cost time

Carried forward:

- **Branches are folders, not versions.** 26 branches, eight unrelated root
  commits, no trunk. `no_sap_reconcile_aws` is the live AWS app;
  `reconcile_public_website` is the marketing site (different AWS account);
  `no_sap_reconcile_gcp` is a GCP port attempt. Confirm the branch before reading
  anything — reading the wrong one produced a wrong finding ("login is broken" was
  true of `no_sap_reconcile` and false of what is deployed).
- **macOS TCC blocks `~/Downloads`, `~/Documents` and `~/Desktop`** from Claude
  Code entirely — even with the sandbox disabled, even for the user's own `!`
  commands. Files must be moved via Finder.
- **A grep for `from 'pkg'` misses dynamic `import('pkg')`.** This produced a
  wrong "apexcharts is unused" claim.
- **Live infrastructure contradicts documentation constantly.** Verify against the
  AWS control plane or a live HTTP request, never against a diagram.

New from 5 Aug:

- **`cd` inside a compound Bash command silently swallows the typecheck.**
  `mkdir … && cd … && ./node_modules/.bin/tsc …` does not run the compiler here
  and does not say so. Run it as its own command, with absolute paths, and read
  the `EXIT:` line. §2.
- **Concurrent authoring diverges within hours, not weeks.** Three specs written
  the same afternoon produced two `ErrorCode` enums disagreeing by thirteen
  members. Nothing noticed until a mechanical cross-file check ran. If two files
  are being written in parallel and share a vocabulary, extract the vocabulary
  *first*.
- **Fixing the model does not fix the contract.** `admittingStepIds` survived
  hours longer in `foundation.openapi.yaml` than in `model/domain.ts`. After a
  model change, grep the four files under `docs/contracts/` before claiming it is
  done.
- **Renaming a type leaves live references behind.** `SupportAccessGrant` →
  `TenantAccessGrant` left seven live references, including invariant 8 in
  `CLAUDE.md` and both support levels in the day-2 escalation ladder. The rule
  applied: rename where the reference is *live*; leave it where the text is
  narrating what the model **used** to be, because that is history and not an
  error. Several such historical references remain by design in
  `docs/tenancy-topology.md`, `docs/model-change-ledger.md` and — since the 6 Aug
  cut — `archive/design-record:docs/swarm/`.
- **Visuals go stale silently and mislead confidently.**
  `docs/user-journeys.html` presented all five gaps as open after three had
  closed the same day — the one artefact that would actually have misled someone.
  It still does; it now carries a banner saying so. `docs/model-topology.html`
  predated the archetype axis, correspondence and the fleet, and still draws about
  ten of the **18** model modules (this said *"sixteen"* until 10 Aug 2026 — the
  trap illustrating itself), and — since 7 Aug — draws dropped types as live.
  After a model change, the HTML is part of the change.
- **A textual coverage check undercounts.** A contract modelling the same concept
  under a different schema name reads as absent. Take the categorical result, not
  the percentage.
- **Duplicate section numbers happen.** `docs/domain-model.md` had two sections
  numbered 12; the audit document that had two numbered 6 is now at
  `archive/design-record:docs/compliance-checklist.md`, and the register that
  replaced it (`docs/infrastructure-risk-register.md`) numbers its findings **K1–K6**
  for exactly this reason (⚠️ *this read K1–K5 until 16 Aug 2026, when **K6** — an
  IAM role named for this project carrying `AdministratorAccess` — was filed from
  live IAM calls; it is the only row in that file verified against AWS since
  4 August*). Cite section *titles* alongside numbers where it
  matters.
- **A citation with no branch qualifier is a dead citation.** *New, 6 Aug, and the
  reason this section grew.* The trunk cut deleted 396 tracked files. Every
  surviving reference to one of them had to be rewritten to name where it went —
  `git show archive/sap-line:src/pages/Drilldown.tsx`, not
  `src/pages/Drilldown.tsx`. Two review passes over the same set of documents each
  declared the sweep exhaustive and each missed the same lines, including the
  first claim `docs/domain-model.md` makes about why it exists. The lesson is
  mechanical: a bare path reads as valid to a human and resolves to nothing, so
  **grep for the path, not for the prose around it**, and re-grep after you think
  you are done. When you write a new citation to anything outside the trunk,
  qualify it with the tag at the moment you write it — retrofitting a qualifier
  is what costs the time.

New from 7 Aug — the v1 sequence:

- ⚠️ **`tools/planner/extract.mjs` is BLIND to most changes, and its silence is
  not evidence of absence.** It indexes **id-shaped field names** (`fooId`,
  `fooIds`, `id`) and branded `Id<'…'>` aliases. It therefore cannot see: a union
  member, a `Record` re-key, a non-id-shaped column, a `@dropped-for-v1` note, an
  exported type alias, an OpenAPI schema, or an enum member. Three of the five
  steps on 7 Aug moved **zero** graph numbers while changing a great deal.
  **The proof is `Membership.role`:** it was a real reference to `Role` for the
  model's entire life and appeared in the graph **not once**, because the field
  was not named `roleId`. Renaming it on 7 Aug added the edge — the +1 was the
  reference becoming *visible*, not the reference being *created*.
  **Consequence, and it is actionable: name a reference field id-shaped.**
  `askedByUserId`, not `askedBy`. A reference named badly is a reference no tool
  here can count. `ResolutionProposal.proposedBy` still has this problem.
- ⚠️ **Piping the typecheck through anything returns the PIPE's exit status.**
  `tsc … | head` reports `head`'s status, which is 0, and it reads exactly like
  success. This is the same trap as `cd` in a compound command, one layer out.
  **Capture the exit code unpiped**, on its own line, and read the `EXIT:` line.
- ⚠️ **A stale contract enum is a transcription, not a decision — fix it the
  first time you see it.** The `sample_data` enum (§5.4) sat on the **access
  path** for two days and was seen and re-reported by three consecutive steps,
  each of which deferred it because deciding "which of thirteen classes belong in
  a grant enum" looked like a judgement call. It was not: the answer was a set
  union of three constants already in `model/governance.ts`. **When you defer a
  finding, write down whether it needs a decision or a derivation.** If it is a
  derivation, it is not deferrable — you are just choosing to ship it wrong.
- ⚠️ **The strongest evidence this repository produces is thrown away every
  time.** Five steps ran between sixteen and twenty-two mechanical checks each —
  model-versus-wire mirror checks, `$ref` resolution, enum ordering — every one of
  them a throwaway shell heredoc, none committed to `tools/`. The compounding
  cost is concrete rather than abstract: a fifty-line checker would have caught
  the `sample_data` enum on 5 Aug, and would today catch
  `CapabilityRequirement` existing in two contract files with two different money
  schemas (§5.3). **`tools/` should be explicitly in scope for the next pass.**
- ⚠️ **A drop note is unverifiable by any tool.** 198 `@dropped-for-v1` markers
  sit above otherwise unchanged declarations. Nothing checks that a note is on the
  right declaration, or that its stated reason is true. Two manual checks in the
  sequence turned on exactly this — confirming `TraceRef` survived so
  `SubjectLocation.trace` still has a writer, and confirming `LegalHold` survived
  so `purgeVerdict()` still reads it. Both held. Neither is mechanically
  re-checkable. Treat §0's counts as evidence about *quantity* and
  `docs/v1-scope-ledger.md` as the only record of *correctness*.

- 🛑 **A HAND `cdk deploy … --exclusively` DEPLOYS THE LOCAL TREE, NOT
  `origin/main` (G4478, 9 Oct 2026).** A checkout that ran `git checkout main`
  and no `git pull` sat at `bf2e13d4`, and its `Data` deploy re-created a
  secret, a policy and a rotation Lambda that #606 had retired. Pinning
  `planeImageTag` to the probe-reported tag pins the IMAGE and says nothing
  about the TEMPLATE. **Before any hand deploy: `git fetch && git pull`, then
  check that `git log -1 --format=%H` equals `git rev-parse origin/main`.**
- ⚠️ **A secret whose value changed is not picked up until the holder
  restarts (G4479).** The pipeline rolls a service only when its image tag
  moves; force a new deployment after the migrate that sets the password.

### The two things that unblock everything else

**1. Build the Dual LLM split — G45, and it is the only decided-but-unbuilt control.**
Three of the six named patterns are built (Action-Selector, Plan-Then-Execute,
Context-Minimization). This is the fourth, it is decided, and **the ERP read path
depends on it**: `EndpointReading.label` and `.value` are text a foreign system
returned, and today nothing separates the agent that reads them from the agent that
proposes a write. G47 stopped that text crossing a TURN boundary; G45 is what stops
it crossing the AGENT boundary within one turn. Until it lands, R5 is mitigated by
argument rather than by construction.
The mechanism is mostly there — `CarriedReading` already demonstrates the shape a
symbolic reference takes. What is missing is a second agent definition and a rule
for what the reader may emit.

## 9. One paragraph for a cold start

ReconcileAI is a reconciliation platform being rebuilt from the ground up as a
multi-tenant, partner-resold product with finance and KYC as worked domains. The
existing application — deleted from the trunk on 6 Aug 2026 and preserved at
`archive/sap-line:src/` — has no authorisation, no domain model and no
tenancy; it is being replaced, not refactored. A canonical model lives in
`model/`, **18** model modules (`ls model/*.ts | wc -l` — it said *"sixteen"* until
10 Aug 2026, with the command beside it), typechecking clean under
settings stricter than that application's own ever were, covering tenancy,
archetypes and procedures, access, governance, policy, correspondence, deployment,
billing, evaluation, observability, a model catalogue, **agents and dashboards**,
and a proposed learning loop. **Since 7 Aug 2026 roughly a third of it is
deliberately inert:** the v1 trim marked 198 top-level exports
`@dropped-for-v1` — declared, no table, no endpoint, no code — and deleted exactly
one thing, the `RoleKey` enum. **§0 is how you tell the two apart**, and
`docs/v1-scope-ledger.md` carries the reasoning. Four OpenAPI tiers and one shared error
vocabulary sit in `docs/contracts/` — 76 operations (⚠️ **72 until 23 Aug 2026**,
before the session tier), **all of them runtime; there
is no administration surface anywhere**, which is the largest single gap.
(⚠️ *Said "Three … 65 operations" until 10 Aug 2026 — see §3's contract table for
the fourth tier. It is `data-plane-local.openapi.yaml`, not the administration
surface, which is still absent.*)
⚠️ **This paragraph said *"Nothing has been built: no AWS resource, no schema, no
code"* until 10 Aug 2026, and two of those three had gone false.** What is built:
a **reconciliation engine that runs** (`model/reconciliation.ts`, pure and total),
**RFC 8785 canonicalisation** (`model/canonical.ts`, G20), **a migration with RLS**
(`db/migrations/`) and a **two-tenant isolation boundary tested against a real
Postgres**, **CI** (`.github/workflows/check.yml`, one gate per G108), and **four
mechanical checkers** in `tools/`, all four inside `npm run check`. 🛑 **The
no-AWS-resource half is STILL TRUE and it is deliberate — G101 put phase one on a
disposable Postgres with an in-process `pg.Pool` and no AWS resource of any kind.**
There is also still **no application, no HTTP surface and no session** — D1 gates
everything with a wire. The data
architecture was decided 4 Aug — two planes separated by database grants, two
topologies (1CloudHub-hosted and customer-owned) running one schema over
PostgreSQL, S3 and an external telemetry backend, with record kind rather than
storage tier determining retention and erasability. The first non-demo customer
is a regulated enterprise sold direct, which makes the customer-owned data plane
a v1 target and puts metering usage in an account we do not control on the
critical path — and a review on 5 Aug retracted the "floor" that was supposed to
bound it, moving the bound inside the signed attestation instead. The work of
5 Aug was access and trust: one grant for delivery and support, an admission gate,
a trifecta rule validated at pack signing, an injection corpus that asserts
absences, autonomy that is measured and recommended but never applied, and a
capability model in which **agents hold no roles**. That evening added the fourth
access axis — **resource class**, thirteen of them, each carrying a rule true of
it and false of its neighbour — and the authorisation spine that makes an
unauthorised act *unrecordable* rather than impossible, joining the audit, read
and metering streams on one identifier for the first time. Six findings from that
pass were open by decision, not oversight; **two closed on 7 Aug** — the
cost-centre and legal-entity columns on `Exception`, and the billing half of the
empty resource classes — and ⚠️ **the claim that *"a canonicalisation scheme is
still not picked, which is now the oldest item in the record with a hard
deadline"* was true for four days and is now false: G20 picked RFC 8785 (JCS) and
it is APPLIED** (`model/canonical.ts`), landed before the first hash, which was
the only window in which it was free. §4.1 lists what remains, and §8
orders it. ⚠️ **§8's own order is superseded by §0a as of 10 Aug 2026:** the
administration contract and the schema are still unblocked, but **D1 — session
establishment, with a gate on tenant selection — is first**, and **G111's money
codec is sequenced ahead of the reader executor** because `canonicalise()` refuses
`bigint`.
